body.text:
1.01a: acintyāvyaktarūpāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane/
1.01b: samastajagadādhāramūrtaye brahmaṇe namaH//
body.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Brahman</s>, whose form is inconceivable, unmanifest, beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) yet whose essence is the <s>guṇas</s>, the embodiment that is the support of the entire universe.

body.text:
1.02a: alpāvaśiṣṭe tu kṛte *mayo nāma mahāsuraH/(B mayanāma)
1.02b: rahasyaṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ jijñāsur jñānam uttamam//
body.translated_text: When only a small portion of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> remained, the great <s>Asura</s> named <s>Maya</s>, desiring to know the supreme, sacred, and secret knowledge,

body.text:
1.03a: vedāṅgam agryam akhilaṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatikāraṇam/
1.03b: ārādhayan vivasvantaṃ tapas tepe suduścaram//
body.translated_text: The foremost <s>Vedāṅga</s> (limb of the Vedas), the complete science of the motions of the luminaries — worshipping <s>Vivasvat</s> (the Sun), he performed exceedingly difficult austerities.

body.text:
1.04a: toṣitas tapasā tena prītas tasmai varārthine/
1.04b: grahāṇāṃ caritaṃ prādān mayāya savitā svayam//
body.translated_text: Pleased and gratified by his austerities, <s>Savitā</s> (the Sun god) himself bestowed upon <s>Maya</s>, who sought that boon, the knowledge of the movements of the planets.

body.text:
1.05a: viditas te *mayā bhāvas toṣitas tapasā hy aham/ (ḍ mayābhāvas)
1.05b: dadyāṃ kālāśrayaṃ jñānaṃ grahāṇāṃ caritaṃ mahat//
body.translated_text: "Your devotion is known to me, O <s>Maya</s>; I am gratified by your austerities. I would give you the great knowledge of the movements of the planets, founded upon time."

body.text:
1.06a: na me tejaHsahaH kaścid ākhyātuṃ nāsti me kṣaṇaH/
1.06b: madaṃśaH puruṣo +ayaṃ te niHśeṣaṃ kathayiṣyati//
body.translated_text: "No one can endure my radiance, nor do I have the leisure to expound it. This person, a portion of myself, shall tell you everything completely."

body.text:
1.07a: ity uktvāntardadhe devaH samādiśyāṃśam ātmanaH/
1.07b: sa pumān mayam āhedaṃ praṇataṃ prāñjalisthitam//
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the god vanished, having appointed a portion of himself. That being then addressed <s>Maya</s>, who stood bowing with palms joined together:

body.text:
1.08a: śṛṇuṣvaikamanāH pūrvaṃ yad uktaṃ jñānam uttamam/
1.08b: yuge yuge maharṣīṇāṃ svayam eva vivasvatā//
body.translated_text: "Listen with single-pointed mind to the supreme knowledge that was formerly spoken by <s>Vivasvat</s> himself to the great sages in each <s>Yuga</s> (age)."

body.text:
1.09a: śāstram ādyaṃ tad evedaṃ yat pūrvaṃ prāha bhāskaraH/
1.09b: yugānāṃ parivartena kālabhedo +atra *kevalaH//(B kevalam)
body.translated_text: "This is that same original <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) which <s>Bhāskara</s> (the Sun) formerly taught. Through the revolution of the <s>Yugas</s>, only the time-difference arises herein."

body.text:
1.10a: lokānām antakṛt kālaH kālo +anyaH kalanātmakaH/
1.10b: sa dvidhā sthūlasūkṣmatvān mūrtaś cāmūrta ucyate//
body.translated_text: Time, the destroyer of worlds, is one kind; time of another kind is that which consists of enumeration. The latter is twofold: by reason of grossness and subtlety, it is called <s>mūrta</s> (manifest) and <s>amūrta</s> (unmanifest).

body.text:
1.11a: prāṇādiH kathito mūrtas truṭyādyo +amūrtasaṃjñakaH/
1.11b: ṣaḍbhiH prāṇair vināḍī syāt tatṣaṣṭyā nāḍikā smṛtā//
body.translated_text: That beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is called <s>mūrta</s> (manifest); that beginning with <s>truṭi</s> is designated <s>amūrta</s> (unmanifest). Six <s>prāṇas</s> make one <s>vināḍī</s>, and sixty of those make one <s>nāḍikā</s> (time unit).

body.text:
1.12a: nāḍīṣaṣṭyā tu nākṣatram ahorātraṃ prakīrtitam/
1.12b: tattriṃśatā bhaven māsaH sāvano +arkodayais tathā//
body.translated_text: Sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> constitute one sidereal day-and-night (<s>nākṣatra ahorātra</s>). Thirty of those make one month; a <s>sāvana</s> (civil) month is reckoned by sunrises.

body.text:
1.13a: aindavas tithibhis tadvat saṃkrāntyā saura ucyate/
1.13b: māsair dvādaśabhir varṣaṃ divyaṃ tad aha ucyate//
body.translated_text: A lunar (<s>aindava</s>) month is reckoned by <s>tithis</s> (lunar days); a solar (<s>saura</s>) month is defined by the Sun's transit (<s>saṃkrānti</s>). Twelve months make a year; that is called a divine day.

body.text:
1.14a: surāsurāṇām anyonyam ahorātraṃ viparyayāt/
1.14b: tatṣaṣṭiH ṣaḍguṇā divyaṃ varṣam āsuram eva ca//
body.translated_text: For the gods and the <s>Asuras</s>, the day-and-night is mutually reversed. Sixty times six of those divine years constitute both a divine year and an <s>Āsura</s> year.

body.text:
1.15a: taddvādaśasahasrāṇi caturyugam udāhṛtam/
1.15b: sūryābdasaṃkhyayā dvitrisāgarair ayutāhataiH//
body.translated_text: Twelve thousand of those constitute a <s>Caturyuga</s> (four-age cycle), which in solar year count equals two-three-oceans multiplied by ten thousand (i.e., 4,320,000 solar years).

body.text:
1.16a: sandhyāsandhyāṃśasahitaṃ vijñeyaṃ taccaturyugam/
1.16b: kṛtādīnāṃ vyavastheyaṃ dharmapādavyavasthayā//
body.translated_text: That <s>Caturyuga</s> is to be understood as including <s>sandhyā</s> (dawn) and <s>sandhyāṃśa</s> (twilight) portions. The arrangement of the <s>Kṛta</s> and other ages follows the arrangement of the feet of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
1.17a: yugasya daśamo bhāgaś catustridvyekasaṅguṇaH/
1.17b: kramāt kṛtayugādīnāṃ ṣaṣṭhāṃśaH sandhyayoH svakaH//
body.translated_text: A tenth part of the <s>Yuga</s>, multiplied successively by four, three, two, and one, gives the duration of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> and the others in order. A sixth part of each is the share of its two <s>sandhyās</s> (dawn and twilight).

body.text:
1.18a: yugānāṃ saptatiH saikā manvantaram ihocyate/
1.18b: *kṛtābdasaṃkhyās tasyānte sandhiH prokto jalaplavaH//(B ṛtābdasaṃkhyā)
body.translated_text: Seventy-one <s>Yugas</s> plus one is called a <s>Manvantara</s> (age of a <s>Manu</s>). At its end, a <s>sandhi</s> (junction) equal in length to a <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> is declared, marked by the great flood.

body.text:
1.19a: sasandhayas te manavaH kalpe jñeyās caturdaśa/
1.19b: kṛtapramāṇaH kalpādau sandhiH pañcadaśaH smṛtaH//
body.translated_text: Those fourteen <s>Manus</s> with their <s>sandhis</s> (junctions) constitute one <s>Kalpa</s>. At the beginning of the <s>Kalpa</s>, a fifteenth <s>sandhi</s> equal in duration to the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> is recognized.

body.text:
1.20a: ittham yugasahasreṇa bhūtasaṃhārakārakaH/
1.20b: kalpo brāhmam ahaH proktaṃ śarvarī tasya tāvatī//
body.translated_text: Thus, by a thousand <s>Yugas</s>, which bring about the dissolution of beings, a <s>Kalpa</s> is declared to be one day of <s>Brahmā</s>; his night is of equal duration.

body.text:
1.21a: paramāyuH śataṃ tasya tayāhorātrasaṃkhyayā/
1.21b: āyuṣo +ardhamitaṃ tasya śeṣakalpo +ayam ādimaH//
body.translated_text: His supreme lifespan is one hundred of those day-and-night reckonings. Half of his life has elapsed; this current <s>Kalpa</s> is the first of the remaining half.

body.text:
1.22a: kalpād asmāc ca manavaH ṣaḍ vyatītāH sasandhayaH/
1.22b: vaivasvatasya ca *manor yugānāṃ trighano gataH//(B manoyugānāṃ)
body.translated_text: From this <s>Kalpa</s>, six <s>Manus</s> with their <s>sandhis</s> have passed. Of the current <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>'s age, twenty-seven <s>Yugas</s> (three cubed) have elapsed.

body.text:
1.23a: aṣṭāviṃśād yugād asmād yātam etat kṛtaṃ yugam/
1.23b: ataH kālaṃ prasaṃkhyāya saṃkhyām ekatra piṇḍayet//
body.translated_text: Of the twenty-eighth <s>Yuga</s>, the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> has passed. From this point, one should reckon the time and consolidate the count into one sum.

body.text:
1.24a: graharkṣadevadaityādi sṛjato +asya carācaram/
1.24b: kṛtādrivedā divyābdāH śataghnā vedhaso gatāH//
body.translated_text: Of <s>Brahmā</s>, who creates this moving and unmoving world of planets, stars, gods, and demons — the divine years elapsed from creation are: <s>Kṛta</s> (4), mountains (7), Vedas (4) multiplied by a hundred (i.e., 47,400 divine years).

body.text:
1.25a: paścād vrajanto +atijavān nakṣatraiH satataṃ grahāH/
1.25b: jīyamānās tu lambante tulyam eva svamārgagāH//
body.translated_text: Moving swiftly westward afterward, the planets are constantly overtaken by the <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms); being thus surpassed, they fall behind, though all moving along their own paths equally.

body.text:
1.26a: prāggatitvam atas teṣāṃ bhagaṇaiH pratyahaṃ gatiH/
1.26b: pariṇāhavaśād bhinnā tadvaśād bhāni bhuñjate//
body.translated_text: Hence their motion is called eastward (<s>prāggati</s>); their daily motion is measured in <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions). Varying due to differences in orbital circumference, they traverse the asterisms accordingly.

body.text:
1.27a: śīghragas tāny athālpena kālena mahatālpagaH/
1.27b: teṣāṃ tu parivartena pauṣṇānte bhagaṇaH smṛtaH//
body.translated_text: A fast-moving planet covers them in a short time, while a slow-moving one takes a great time. The completion of one full revolution ending at <s>Revati</s> (the last <s>nakṣatra</s>) is called one <s>bhagaṇa</s> (complete revolution).

body.text:
1.28a: vikalānāṃ kalā ṣaṣṭyā tatṣaṣṭyā bhāga ucyate/
1.28b: tattriṃśatā bhaved rāśir bhagaṇo dvādaśaiva te//
body.translated_text: Sixty <s>vikalās</s> (arc-seconds) make one <s>kalā</s> (arc-minute); sixty of those make one <s>bhāga</s> (degree). Thirty degrees make one <s>rāśi</s> (zodiacal sign); twelve of those constitute one <s>bhagaṇa</s> (full revolution of 360°).

body.text:
1.29a: yuge sūryajñaśukrāṇām khacatuṣkaradārṇavāH/
1.29b: kujārkiguruśīghrāṇāṃ bhagaṇāH pūrvayāyinām//
body.translated_text: In a <s>Yuga</s>, the <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions) of the Sun (<s>Sūrya</s>), Mercury (<s>Jña</s>), and Venus (<s>Śukra</s>) moving eastward are: space-four-four-ocean (i.e., 4,320,000).

body.text:
1.30a: indo rasāgnitritrīṣusaptabhūdharamārgaṇāH/(57753336)
1.30b: dasratryaṣṭarasāṅkākṣilocanāni kujasya tu//(2296832) checked
body.translated_text: The Moon's (<s>Indu</s>) revolutions are: liquids-fire-three-three-arrows-seven-mountains-earth (57,753,336). And those of Mars (<s>Kuja</s>) are: Aśvins-three-eight-liquids-limbs-eyes-eyes (2,296,832).

body.text:
1.31a: budhaśīghrasya śūnyartukhādritryaṅkanagendavaH/(17937060)
1.31b: bṛhaspateH khadasrākṣivedaṣaḍvahnayas tathā//(364220)
body.translated_text: The revolutions of Mercury's <s>śīghra</s> (fast epicycle) are: zero-seasons-space-mountains-three-limbs-lords-of-mountains (17,937,060). Those of Jupiter (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) are: space-Aśvins-eyes-Vedas-six-fires (364,220).

body.text:
1.32a: sitaśīghrasya ṣaṭsaptatriyamāśvikhabhūdharāH/(7022376)
1.32b: śaner bhujaṅgaṣaṭpañcarasavedaniśākarāH//(146568)
body.translated_text: The revolutions of Venus's <s>śīghra</s> (fast epicycle) are: six-seven-three-Yamas-Aśvins-space-mountains (7,022,376). Those of Saturn (<s>Śani</s>) are: serpents-six-five-liquids-Vedas-moon (146,568).

body.text:
1.33a: candroccasyāgniśūnyāśvivasusarpārṇavā yuge/(488203)
1.33b: vāmaṃ pātasya vasvagniyamāśviśikhidasrakāH//(232238)
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the lunar apogee (<s>candroccā</s>) in a <s>Yuga</s> are: fire-zero-Aśvins-Vasus-serpents-oceans (488,203). Retrograde, the revolutions of the lunar node (<s>Pāta</s>) are: Vasus-fire-Yamas-Aśvins-flames-Aśvins (232,238).

body.text:
1.34a: bhānām aṣṭākṣivasvadritridvidvyaṣṭaśarendavaH/(1582237828)
1.34b: bhodayā bhagaṇaiH svaiH svair ūnāH svasvodayā yuge//
body.translated_text: The risings of the asterisms (<s>bhāni</s>) are: eight-eyes-Vasus-mountains-three-two-two-eight-moon (1,582,237,828). The risings in a <s>Yuga</s> diminished by the respective <s>bhagaṇas</s> of each planet give that planet's own risings.

body.text:
1.35a: bhavanti śaśino māsāH sūryendubhagaṇāntaram/
1.35b: ravimāsonitās te tu śeṣāH syur adhimāsakāH//
body.translated_text: The lunar months equal the difference between the <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions) of the Sun and the Moon. Those lunar months diminished by the solar months give the remainder as <s>adhimāsakas</s> (intercalary months).

body.text:
1.36a: sāvahāhāni cāndrebhyo dyubhyaH projjhya tithikṣayāH/
1.36b: udayād udayaṃ bhānor bhūmisāvanavāsaraH//
body.translated_text: The civil (<s>sāvana</s>) days are obtained from the lunar days by subtracting <s>tithikṣaya</s> (omitted lunar days). From sunrise to sunrise of the Sun is one terrestrial civil day (<s>bhūmisāvanavāsara</s>).

body.text:
1.37a: vasudvyaṣṭādrirūpāṅkasaptādritithayo yuge/(1577917828)
1.37b: cāndrāH khāṣṭakhakhavyomakhāgnikhartuniśākarāH//(1603000080)
body.translated_text: The <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) in a <s>Yuga</s> are: Vasus-two-eight-mountains-forms-limbs-seven-mountains (1,577,917,828). The lunar days (<s>cāndra</s>) are: space-eight-space-space-sky-space-fire-space-seasons-moon (1,603,000,080).

body.text:
1.38a: ṣaḍvahnitrihutāśāṅkatithayaś cādhimāsakāH/(1593336)
1.38b: tithikṣayā yamārthāśvidvyaṣṭavyomaśarāśvinaH//(25082252)
body.translated_text: The intercalary months (<s>adhimāsaka</s>) as <s>tithis</s> are: six-fire-three-fire-limbs (1,593,336). The omitted lunar days (<s>tithikṣaya</s>) are: Yamas-objects-Aśvins-two-eight-sky-arrows-Aśvins (25,082,252).

body.text:
1.39a: khacatuṣkasamudrāṣṭakupañca ravimāsakāH/(51840000)
1.39b: bhavanti bhodayā bhānubhagaṇair ūnitāH kvahāH//
body.translated_text: The solar months are: space-four-four-oceans-eight-five (51,840,000). The civil days are obtained from the risings of the asterisms diminished by the Sun's <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions).

body.text:
1.40a: adhimāsonarātryārkṣacāndrasāvanavāsarāH/
1.40b: ete sahasraguṇitāH kalpe syur bhagaṇādayaH//
body.translated_text: The sidereal (<s>ārkṣa</s>), lunar (<s>cāndra</s>), and civil (<s>sāvana</s>) days diminished by the intercalary month days — all these <s>bhagaṇas</s> and other quantities, multiplied by a thousand, give the values for a <s>Kalpa</s>.

body.text:
1.41a: prāggateH sūryamandasya kalpe saptāṣṭavahnayaH/(387)
1.41b: kaujasya vedakhayamā baudhasyāṣṭartuvahnayaH//(204, 368)
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the Sun's <s>mandocca</s> (apogee, slow epicycle) in a <s>Kalpa</s> are: seven-eight-fires (387). For Mars (<s>Kuja</s>): Vedas-space-Yamas (204). For Mercury (<s>Budha</s>): eight-seasons-fires (368).

body.text:
1.42a: khakharandhrāṇi jaivasya śaukrasyārthaguṇeṣavaH/(900, 535)
1.42b: go +agnayaH śanimandasya pātānām atha vāmataH//(39)
body.translated_text: For Jupiter (<s>Jaiva</s>, i.e., <s>Bṛhaspati</s>): space-space-nine (900). For Venus (<s>Śaukra</s>): objects-qualities-arrows (535). For Saturn (<s>Śani</s>): cows-fires (39). Now the nodes (<s>pātas</s>), moving retrograde:

body.text:
1.43a: manudasrās tu kaujasya baudhasyāṣṭāṣṭasāgarāH/ (214, 488)
1.43b: kṛtādricandrā jaivasya trikhāṅkāś ca tathā bhṛgos //(ḍ bhṛgos tathā)(174, 903)
body.translated_text: For Mars (<s>Kuja</s>): <s>Manus</s>-Aśvins (214). For Mercury (<s>Budha</s>): eight-eight-oceans (488). For Jupiter (<s>Jaiva</s>): <s>Kṛta</s>-mountains-moon (174). And likewise for Venus (<s>Bhṛgu</s>): three-space-limbs (903).

body.text:
1.44a: śanipātasya bhagaṇāH kalpe yamarasartavaH/(662)
1.44b: bhagaṇāH pūrvam evātra proktāś candroccapātayoH//
body.translated_text: The <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions) of Saturn's node (<s>Śani-pāta</s>) in a <s>Kalpa</s> are: Yamas-liquids-seasons (662). The <s>bhagaṇas</s> of the lunar apogee (<s>candroccā</s>) and lunar node have already been stated above.

body.text:
1.45a: ṣaṇmanūnāṃ tu sampīḍya kālaṃ tatsandhibhiH saha/
1.45b: kalpādisandhinā sārdhaṃ vaivasvatamanos tathā//
body.translated_text: Compressing the time of the six past <s>Manus</s> together with their <s>sandhis</s> (junctions), along with the <s>sandhi</s> at the beginning of the <s>Kalpa</s>, and also of the current <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>'s period —

body.text:
1.46a: yugānām trighanaṃ yātaṃ tathā kṛtayugaṃ tv idam/
1.46b: projjhya sṛṣṭes tataH kālaṃ pūrvoktaṃ divyasaṃkhyayā//
body.translated_text: Twenty-seven <s>Yugas</s> (three cubed) have elapsed, and also this <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>. Subtracting then the previously stated time from creation in divine year count,

body.text:
1.47a: sūryābdasaṃkhyayā jñeyāH kṛtasyānte gatā amī/
1.47b: khacatuṣkayamādryagniśararandhraniśākarāH//(1953720000)
body.translated_text: The solar years elapsed at the end of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> are to be known as: space-four-four-Yamas-mountains-fire-arrows-holes-moon (1,953,720,000).

body.text:
1.48a: ata ūrdhvam amī yuktā gatakālābdasaṃkhyayā/
1.48b: māsīkṛtā yutā māsair madhuśuklādibhir gataiH//
body.translated_text: To this, the elapsed year count of the current age is to be added. Converting to months and adding the elapsed months from <s>Madhu</s> (Caitra) and <s>Śukla</s> (bright fortnight) onward,

body.text:
1.49a: pṛthakṣthās te +adhimāsaghnāH sūryamāsavibhājitāH/
1.49b: labdhādhimāsakair yuktā dinīkṛtya dinānvitāH//
body.translated_text: Those placed separately are multiplied by the intercalary month factor and divided by solar months. The resulting intercalary months are added, then the whole is converted to days and the elapsed days are added.

body.text:
1.50a: dviṣṭhās tithikṣayābhyastāś cāndravāsarabhājitāH/
1.50b: labdhonarātrirahitā laṅkāyām ārdharātrikaH//
body.translated_text: Placed in two positions, multiplied by the <s>tithikṣaya</s> (omitted days) factor and divided by lunar days — the result is subtracted from the elapsed nights: this gives the midnight reckoning at <s>Laṅkā</s>.

body.text:
1.51a: sāvano dyugaṇaH sūryād dinamāsābdapās tataH/
1.51b: saptabhiH kṣayitaH śeṣaH sūryādyo vāsareśvaraH//
body.translated_text: This is the civil (<s>sāvana</s>) day-count (<s>dyugaṇa</s>). From it the lords of the day, month, and year are derived from the Sun. Dividing by seven, the remainder gives the lord of the weekday, beginning with <s>Sūrya</s> (Sunday).

body.text:
1.52a: māsābdadinasaṃkhyāptaṃ dvitrighnaṃ rūpasaṃyutam/
1.52b: saptoddhṛtāvaśeṣau tu vijñeyau māsavarṣau//
body.translated_text: The number of months, years, and days is respectively multiplied by two and three, and unity is added. Dividing by seven, the two remainders give the lords of the month and the year respectively.

body.text:
1.53a: yathā svabhaganābhyasto dinarāśiH kuvāsaraiH/
1.53b: vibhājito madhyagatyā bhagaṇādir graho bhavet//
body.translated_text: When the accumulated day-count, multiplied by a planet's own <s>bhagaṇas</s> (revolutions), is divided by the civil days of the <s>Yuga</s>, the result — in <s>bhagaṇas</s>, signs, degrees, and so on — gives the planet's mean position.

body.text:
1.54a: evaṃ svaśīghramandoccā ye proktāH pūrvayāyinaH/
1.54b: vilomagatayaH pātās tadvac cakrād viśodhitāH//
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>śīghra</s> (fast), <s>manda</s> (slow), and <s>ucca</s> (apex) [anomalies] previously described move in the reverse direction; the nodes (<s>pāta</s>) are similarly subtracted from the revolution [total]. // The revolutions of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), multiplied by twelve, added with the current signs (<s>rāśi</s>) and purified, when divided by sixty, yield the [Jupiter] years beginning with <s>Vijaya</s> and so on. //

body.text:
1.55a: dvādaśaghnā guror yātā bhagaṇā vartamānakaiH/
1.55b: rāśibhiH sahitāH śuddhāH ṣaṣṭyā syur vijayādayaH//
body.translated_text: This has been stated in detail; in brief, the practical mean motion (<s>madhyamānayana</s>) of the planets is to be computed from the desired point within the <s>yuga</s>. //

body.text:
1.56a: vistareṇaitad uditaṃ saṃkṣepād vyāvahārikam/
1.56b: madhyamānayanaṃ kāryaṃ grahāṇām iṣṭato yugāt//
body.translated_text: At the end of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> in this [system], all the planets are at their mean positions; except for the nodes, <s>manda</s>-apexes, [and <s>śīghra</s>-apexes], they have reached equality at the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries). //

body.text:
1.57a: asmin kṛtayugasyānte sarve madhyagatā grahāH/
1.57b: *vinā tu pātamandoccān meṣādau tulyatām itāH (ḍ vinendu)//
body.translated_text: The lunar apex (<s>śaśāṅkocca</s>) is at the beginning of <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn); its node is at the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra); the others, having reached zero degrees, are not mentioned [because they are] slow-moving. //

body.text:
1.58a: makarādau śaśāṅkoccaṃ tatpātas tu tulādigaH/
1.58b: niraṃśatvam gatāś cānye noktās te mandacāriṇaH//
body.translated_text: The earth's radius is eight hundred <s>yojanas</s>; doubled [gives the diameter]. From the square of that, multiplied by ten, the square root is the earth's circumference. //

body.text:
1.59a: yojanāni śatāny aṣṭau bhūkarṇo dviguṇāni tu/
1.59b: tadvargato daśaguṇāt padaṃ bhūparidhir bhavet//
body.translated_text: The true circumference of the earth at one's own [latitude] is obtained by multiplying the [standard] circumference by the cosine (<s>lambajyā</s>) and dividing by the radius (<s>trijīvā</s>). The daily motion of a planet, multiplied by the longitude difference and divided [by the circumference], //

body.text:
1.60a: lambajyāghnas trijīvāptaH sphuṭo bhūparidhiH svakaH/
1.60b: tena deśāntarābhyastā grahabhuktir vibhājitā//
body.translated_text: gives the correction in minutes, etc. In the east, it is to be subtracted from the planets; when the location is west of the prime meridian, it is to be added — [these are] the [positions] for one's own location. //

body.text:
1.61a: kalādi tat phalaṃ prācyāṃ grahebhyaH pariśodhayet/
1.61b: rekhāpratīcīsaṃsthāne prakṣipet syuH svadeśajā//
body.translated_text: On the mid-line between the abode of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> and the city of the gods are [the places]: <s>Rohītaka</s>, <s>Avantī</s>, and the lake <s>Sannihita</s>. //

body.text:
1.62a: rākṣasālayadevaukaHśailayor madhyasūtragāH/
1.62b: rohītakam avantī ca yathā sannihitaṃ saraH//
body.translated_text: When the observed [rising of the] moon occurs after [the time of] its calculated [rising], then one's location is east of the mid-line. //

body.text:
1.63a: atītyonmīlanād indoH paścāt tadgaṇitāgatāt/(C atītyonmīlanād indor dṛkṣiddhir gaṇitāgatāt/)
1.63b: yadā bhavet tadā prācyāṃ svasthānaṃ madhyato bhavet//
body.translated_text: And if it occurs before, or likewise with the setting, then [the same conclusion follows]. By the interval in <s>nāḍīs</s> between the two, multiply the true circumference of the earth. //

body.text:
1.64a: aprāpya ca bhavet paścād evaṃ vāpi nimīlanāt/
1.64b: tayor antaranāḍībhir hanyād bhūparidhiṃ sphuṭam//
body.translated_text: Dividing by sixty, the result in <s>yojanas</s> — either east or west — [determines] one's location on the circumference. From these, one should compute the longitude difference. //

body.text:
1.65a: ṣaṣṭyā vibhajya labdhais tu yojanaiH prāg athāparaiH/
1.65b: svadeśaH paridhau jñeyaH kuryād deśāntaraṃ hi taiH//
body.translated_text: In an eastern location, the commencement of the [new] day occurs when the midnight is more [than at the meridian]; by the <s>nāḍīs</s> of that longitude difference, [the time is adjusted]. In the west, when [midnight is] less, one should indicate [accordingly]. //

body.text:
1.66a: vārapravṛttiH prāgdeśe kṣapārdhe +abhyadhike bhavet/
1.66b: taddeśāntaranāḍībhiH paścād ūne vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: The daily motion multiplied by the desired <s>nāḍīs</s> and divided by sixty gives [the correction] in minutes, etc. It is to be subtracted from the elapsed [motion] and added to the remaining [motion], yielding the instantaneous [position]. //

body.text:
1.67a: iṣṭanāḍīguṇā bhuktiH ṣaṣṭyā bhaktā kalādikam/
1.67b: gate śodhyaṃ yutaṃ gamye kṛtvā tātkāliko bhavet//
body.translated_text: The maximum north-south declination is one-eightieth of the degrees in the zodiacal circle. The cold-rayed one (Moon) is deflected from the end of its own declination by its own node. //

body.text:
1.68a: bhacakraliptāśītyaṃśaṃ paramaṃ dakṣiṇottaram/
1.68b: vikṣipyate svapātena svakrāntyantād anuṣṇaguH//
body.translated_text: Nine-tenths of that, doubled, for <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter); tripled for <s>Kuja</s> (Mars). <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and the son of the Sun (Saturn) are deflected by their nodes [by] four times [that amount]. //

body.text:
1.69a: tannavāṃśaṃ dviguṇitaṃ jīvas triguṇitaṃ kujaH/
1.69b: budhaśukrārkajāH pātair vikṣipyante caturguṇam//
body.translated_text: Thus, [the maximum latitudes] stated in succession for the Moon and the rest are 270, 120, 90, 120, 120, multiplied by ten — [these are] the mean maximum latitude values in arc-minutes. //

body.text:
1.70a: evam trighanarandhrārkarasārkārkā daśāhatāH/
1.70b: candrādīnāṃ kramād uktā madhyavikeṣepaliptikāH//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on True Positions (<s>spaṣṭādhikāra</s>)] The invisible forms attached to the zodiac, known as the <s>śīghra</s>, <s>manda</s>, <s>ucca</s>, and <s>pāta</s>, are the causes of the planets' motion. //

body.text:
[spaṣṭādhikāraH]
2.01a: adṛśyarūpāH kālasya mūrtayo bhagaṇāśritāH/
2.01b: śīghramandoccapātākhyā grahāṇāṃ gatihetavaH//
body.translated_text: Bound by their wind-rays (<s>vātaraśmi</s>), [the planets] are pulled by them eastward and westward with their right and left hands, each toward its own direction as [the attracting point] is near. //

body.text:
2.02a: tadvātaraśmibhir *baddhās tais savyetarapāṇibhiH/ (C naddhās)
2.02b: prāk paścād apakṛṣyante yathāsannaṃ svadiṅmukham//
body.translated_text: The wind called <s>Pravaha</s> impels them toward their own apex (<s>svocca</s>). Pulled east and west, they move in various ways. //

body.text:
2.03a: pravahākhyo marut tāṃs tu svoccābhimukham īrayet/
2.03b: pūrvāparākṛṣṭās te *gatiṃ yānti pṛthagvidhāH//(C gatīr, pṛthagvidhām)
body.translated_text: The apex, situated in the first half of the zodiac from the planet, pulls the planet forward (eastward). Situated in the latter half, it pulls the planet backward (westward). //

body.text:
2.04a: grahāt prāgbhagaṇārdhasthaH prāṅmukhaṃ karṣati graham/
2.04b: uccasaṃjño +aparārdhasthas tadvat paścānmukhaṃ graham//
body.translated_text: When the planets, pulled by the apex, move forward through the zodiac, that is called positive (<s>dhana</s>); when backward, it is called negative (<s>ṛṇa</s>). //

body.text:
2.05a: svoccāpakṛṣṭā *bhagaṇaiH prāṅmukhaṃ yānti yad grahāH/ (C bhagaṇāt)
2.05b: tat teṣu dhanam ity uktam ṛṇaṃ paścānmukheṣu *ca// (tu)
body.translated_text: Similarly, the node (<s>Rāhu</s>), from the south and north, with its own velocity, deflects [the planets]; it imparts the deflection (latitude) to the Moon and the others, [measured] from their declination. //

body.text:
2.06a: *dakṣiṇottarato +apy evaṃ pāto *rāhuH svaraṃhasā/(C dakṣiṇottarayor, rāhuś ca raṃhasā)
2.06b: vikṣipaty eṣa vikṣepaṃ candrādīnām apakramāt//
body.translated_text: The node, when in the latter half [of the zodiac from the planet], deflects the planet northward; when in the first half, it pulls it southward. //

body.text:
2.07a: uttarābhimukhaṃ pāto vikṣipaty aparārdhagaH/
2.07b: grahaṃ prāgbhagaṇārdhastho yāmyāyām apakarṣati//
body.translated_text: For <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), when the node is situated relative to the <s>śīghra</s> [apex] in the same way, due to the attraction of that <s>śīghra</s>, those two are deflected as described. //

body.text:
2.08a: budhabhārgavayoH śīghrāt tadvat pāto *yadā sthitaH/ (C yathāsthitaH)
2.08b: tacchīghrākarṣaṇāt tau tu vikṣipyete yathoktavat//
body.translated_text: Because of the greatness of its orbit, the Sun is pulled only a little; because of the smallness of its orbit, the Moon is pulled greatly. //

body.text:
2.09a: mahatvān maṇḍalasyārkaH svalpam evāpakṛṣyate/
2.09b: maṇḍalālpatayā candras tato bahv apakṛṣyate/
body.translated_text: <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars) and the others, because of their small physical size, are pulled very far and with great speed by the beings called <s>śīghra</s>, <s>manda</s>, and <s>ucca</s>. //

body.text:
2.10a: bhaumādayo +alpamūrtitvāc chīghramandoccasañjñakaiH/ (C saṃjñitaiH)
2.10b: daivatair apakṛṣyante sudūram ativegitāH//
body.translated_text: Therefore, their positive and negative [corrections] become very great, due to [variations in] velocity. Thus pulled by these [forces], they move through the sky, driven by the wind. //

body.text:
2.11a: ato dhanarṇaṃ sumahat teṣāṃ gativaśād bhavet/
2.11b: ākṛṣyamāṇās tair evaṃ vyomni yānty anilāhatāH//
body.translated_text: Retrograde, very retrograde, slow, very slow, even-paced, fast, very fast — the motion of the planets is eightfold. //

body.text:
2.12a: *vakrātivakrā vikalā mandā mandatarā samā/ (C vakrānuvakrā)
2.12b: tathā śīghratarā śīghrā grahāṇām aṣṭadhā gatiH//
body.translated_text: Among these, very fast, fast, [even-paced], slow, very slow, and direct — these five are known. That which is retrograde [includes] the very retrograde. //

body.text:
2.13a: tatrātiśīghrā śīghrākhyā mandā mandatarā samā/
2.13b: ṛjvīti pañcadhā jñeyā *yā vakrā sātivakragā//(C +anyā vakrādikā matā)
body.translated_text: Due to their respective velocities, the planets always attain positions corresponding to observation — that process of making [positions] true (<s>sphuṭīkaraṇa</s>) I shall now explain with care. //

body.text:
2.14a: tattadgativaśān nityaṃ yathā dṛktulyatāṃ grahāH/
2.14b: prayānti tat pravakṣyāmi sphuṭīkaraṇam ādarāt//
body.translated_text: One-eighth of a sign in arc-minutes is called the first half-<s>jyā</s> (half-sine). That, diminished by the quotient [obtained by] dividing it by itself, and combined, is the second [half-sine]. //

body.text:
2.15a: rāśiliptāṣṭamo bhāgaH prathamaṃ jyārdham ucyate/
2.15b: tat tadvibhaktalabdhonamiśritaṃ tad dvitīyakam//
body.translated_text: Dividing the successive sums by the first [half-sine] in order, the results diminished and added [alternately] give the twenty-four half-sine values (<s>jyārdhapiṇḍa</s>) in order. //

body.text:
2.16a: ādyenaivaṃ kramāt piṇḍān bhaktvā *labdhonasaṃyutāH/(C labdhonitair yutaiH)
2.16b: *khaṇḍakāH syuś caturviṃśajyārdhapiṇḍāH kramād amī//(C khaṇḍakais)
body.translated_text: [The first twelve half-sine values are:] 224, 449, 691, 890, 1105, 1315, //

body.text:
2.17a: tattvāśvino +aṅkābdhikṛtā rūpabhūmidharartavaH/(224, 449, 691)
2.17b: khāṅkāṣṭau pañcaśūnyeśā bāṇarūpaguṇendavaH//(890, 1105, 1315)

2.18a: śūnyalocanapañcaikāś chidrarūpamunīndavaH/(1520, 1719)
2.18b: viyaccandrātidhṛtayo guṇarandhrāmbarāśvinaH//(1910, 2093)

2.19a: muniṣaḍyamanetrāṇi candrāgnikṛtadasrakāH/(2267, 2431)
2.19b: pañcāṣṭaviṣayākṣīṇi kuñjarāśvinagāśvinaH//(2585, 2728)

2.20a: randhrapañcāṣṭakayamā vasvadryaṅkayamās tathā/(2859, 2978)
2.20b: kṛtāṣṭaśūnyajvalanā nagādriśaśivahnayaH//(3084, 3179)

2.21a: ṣaṭpañcalocanaguṇāś candranetrāgnivahnayaH/(3256, 3321)
2.21b: yamādrivahnijvalanā randhraśūnyārnavāgnayaH//(3372), 3401)
body.translated_text: 3431, 3438. These are the half-sine sums in the forward direction, subtracting [successively] from the radius (<s>vyāsārdha</s>), [giving] the versed-sine values. //

body.text:
2.22a: rūpāgnisāgaraguṇā vasvagnikṛtavahnayaH/(3431, 3438)
2.22b: projjhyotkrameṇa vyāsārdhād utkramajyārdhapiṇḍikāH//
body.translated_text: [The versed-sine values are:] 7, 29, 66, 117, 182, 261, 354, //

body.text:
2.23a: munayo randhrayamalā rasaṣaṭkā munīśvarāH/(7, 29, 66, 117)
2.23b: dvyaṣṭaikā rūpaṣaḍdasrāH sāgarārthahutāśanāH/(182, 261, 354)

2.24a: khartuvedā navādryarthā diṅnāgās tryarthakuñjarāH/(460, 710, 853)
2.24b: nagāmbaraviyaccandrā rūpabhūdharaśaṅkarāH//(1007, 1171)

2.25a: śarārṇavahutāśaikā bhujaṅgākṣiśarendavaH/(1345, 1528)
2.25b: navarūpamahīdhraikā gajaikāṅkaniśākarāH//1719, 1918)

2.26a: guṇāśvirūpanetrāṇi pāvakāgniguṇāśvinaH/(2123, 2333)
2.26b: vasvarṇavārthayamalās turaṅgartunagāśvinaH//(2548, 2767)
body.translated_text: 2989, 3293, 3438 — these are the versed-sine sums. //

body.text:
2.27a: navāṣṭanavanetrāṇi pāvakaikayamāgnayaH/(2989, 3293)
2.27b: gajāgnisāgaraguṇā utkramajyārdhapiṇḍakāH//(3438)
body.translated_text: The <s>jyā</s> (sine) of the maximum declination is 1397. The <s>jyā</s> multiplied by that and divided by the radius gives the arc of declination. //

body.text:
2.28a: paramāpakramajyā tu saptarandhraguṇendavaH/(1397)
2.28b: tadguṇā jyā trijīvāptā taccāpaṃ krāntir ucyate//(C iṣyate)
body.translated_text: Having corrected the planet from the <s>manda-ucca</s> (slow apex) and having corrected from the <s>śīghra</s> (fast apex) as well, the remainder is the anomaly (<s>kendra</s>); from that, [compute] the base-sine (<s>bhujajyā</s>) and the perpendicular-sine (<s>koṭi</s>). //

body.text:
2.29a: grahaṃ saṃśodhya mandoccāt tathā śīghrād viśodhya ca/
2.29b: śeṣaṃ kendrapadaṃ tasmād bhujajyā koṭir eva ca//(C kendraṃ padaṃ)
body.translated_text: In odd quadrants, the base-sine [is computed] from the elapsed [arc] and the perpendicular from the remaining [arc]; in even quadrants, the base-sine from the remaining and the perpendicular from the elapsed. //

body.text:
2.30a: gatād bhujajyā viṣame gamyāt koṭiH pade bhavet/
2.30b: *yugme tu gamyād bāhujyā koṭijyā tu gatād bhavet//(C same)
body.translated_text: The arc-minutes divided by 225 give the [index for the] sine-sum in the elapsed [table]. The [difference] between the elapsed and the next [value], multiplied [by the remainder] and divided by 225, //

body.text:
2.31a: liptās tattvayamair bhaktā *labdhaṃ jyāpiṇḍikaṃ gatām/(C labdhā jyāpiṇḍikā gatāH)
2.31b: gatagamyāntarābhyastaṃ vibhajet tattvalocanaiH//(225)
body.translated_text: gives the result to be added to the sine-sum of the elapsed [index]. This is the procedure for the direct sine; it is also prescribed for the versed sine. //

body.text:
2.32a: tadavāptaphalaṃ yojyaṃ jyāpiṇḍe *gatasaṃjñake/(C gatasaṃjñite)
2.32b: syāt kramajyāvidhir ayaṃ utkramajyāsv api smṛtaH//

2.33a: jyāṃ *projjhya śeṣaṃ tattvāśvihataṃ tadvivaroddhṛtam/(C projjhyānyattattvayamair hatvā)(225)
2.33b: saṃkhyātattvāśvisaṃvarge *saṃyojya dhanur ucyate//(C saṃyojyaṃ) (225)

2.34a: raver mandaparidhyaṃśā manavaH śītago radāH/ (14, 32)
3.34b: yugmānte viṣamānte tu nakhaliptonitās tayoH//

2.35a: yugmānte +arthādrayaH *khāgnisurāH sūryā navārṇavāH/(C khāgniH surās)(75, 30, 33, 12, 49)
2.35b: oje dvyagā vasuyamā radā rudrā gajābdayaH//

2.36a: kujādīnāṃ *ataH śīghrā yugmānte +arthāgnidasrakāH/(C tataś śaighryā)(235)
2.36b: guṇāgnicandrāH *khanagā dvirasākṣīṇi go+agnayaH//(C khāgāś ca)(133, 70, 262, 39)

2.37a: ojānte *dvitriyamalā dviviśve yamaparvatāH/(C dvitrikayamāH)(132, 72)
2.37b: khartudasrā viyadvedāH śīghrakarmaṇi kīrtitāH//(260,40)

2.38a: ojayugmāntaraguṇā bhujajyā trijyayoddhṛtā/
2.38b: *yugme vṛtte dhanarṇaṃ syād ojād ūnādhike sphuṭam// (C yugmavṛtte)

2.39a: tadguṇe bhujakoṭijye bhagaṇāṃśavibhājite/
2.39b: tadbhujajyāphaladhanur māndaṃ liptādikaṃ phalam//

2.40a: *śaighryaṃ koṭiphalaṃ kendre makarādau dhanaṃ smṛtam/(C śaighre)
2.40b: saṃśodhyaṃ tu *trijīvāyāṃ karkyādau koṭijaṃ phalam//(C trijīvātaH)

2.41a: tadbāhuphalavargaikyān mūlaṃ karṇaś calābhidhaH/
2.41b: trijyābhyastaṃ bhujaphalaṃ calakarṇavibhājitam//

2.42a: labdhasya cāpaṃ liptādiphalaṃ *śaighryam idaṃ smṛtam/ (C śaighram)
2.42b: etad ādye kujādīnāṃ caturthe caiva karmaṇi//

2.43a: māndaṃ karmaikam arkendor bhaumādīnām athocyate/
2.43b: *śaighryaṃ māndaṃ punar māndaṃ śaighryaṃ catvāry anukramāt//(C śaighraṃ)

2.44a: madhye śīghraphalasyārdhaṃ māndam ardhaphalaṃ tathā/
2.44b: madhyagrahe *mandaphalaṃ sakalaṃ śaighryam eva ca//(C punar māndaṃ)

2.45a: ajādikendre sarveṣāṃ *śaighrye mānde ca karmaṇi/(C mānde śaighre)
2.45b: dhanaṃ grahāṇāṃ liptādi tulādāv rṇam eva ca//

2.46a: arkabāhuphalābhyastā grahabhuktir vibhājitā/
2.46b: bhacakrakalikābhis tu liptāH karyā grahe +arkavat//

2.47a: svamandabhuktisaṃśuddhā madhyabhuktir niśāpateH/
2.47b: dorjyāntarādikaṃ kṛtvā bhuktāv ṛṇadhanaṃ bhavet//

2.48a: grahabhukteH phalaṃ kāryaṃ grahavan mandakarmaṇi/
2.48b: dorjyāntaraguṇā bhuktis tattvanetroddhṛtā punaH// (225)

2.49a: svamandaparidhikṣuṇṇā bhagaṇāṃśoddhṛtā kalāH/]
2.49b: karkyādau tu dhanaṃ tatra makarādāv ṛṇaṃ smṛtam//

2.50a: mandasphuṭīkṛtāṃ bhuktiṃ projjhya śīghroccabhuktitaH/
2.50b: taccheśaṃ vivareṇātha hanyāt trijyāntyakarṇayoH//

2.51a: calakarṇahṛtaṃ bhuktau karṇe trijyādhike dhanam/
2.51b: ṛṇam ūne +adhike projjhya śeṣaṃ vakragatir bhavet//

2.52a: dūrasthitaH svaśīghroccād grahaH śithilaraśmibhiH/
2.52b: savyetarākṛṣtatanur bhavet vakragatis tadā//

2.53a: kṛtartucandrair vedendraiH śūnyatryekair guṇāṣṭabhiH/(164, 144, 130, 83)
2.53b: śararudraiś caturtheṣu kendrāṃśair bhūsutādayaH//(115)

2.54a: bhavanti vakriṇas tais tu svaiH svaiś cakrād viśodhitaiH/
2.54b: avaśiṣṭāṃśatulyaiH svaiH kendrair ujjhanti vakratām//

2.55a: mahattvāc chīghraparidheH saptame bhṛgubhūsutau/
2.55b: aṣṭame jīvaśaśaijau navame tu śanaiścaraH//

2.56a: kujārkigurupātānāṃ grahavac chīghrajaṃ phalam/
2.56b: vāmaṃ tṛtīyakaṃ māndaṃ budhabhārgavayoH phalam//

2.57a: svapātonād grahāj jīvā śīghrād bhṛgujasaumyayoH/
2.57b: vikṣepaghny antyakarṇāptā vikṣepas trijyayā vidhoH//

2.58a: vikṣepāpakramaikatve krāntir vikṣepasaṃyutā/
2.58b: digbhede viyutā spaṣṭā bhāskarasya yathāgatā//

2.59a: grahodayaprāṇahatā khakhāṣṭaikoddhṛtā gatiH/
2.59b: cakrāsavo labdhayutā svāhorātrāsavaH smṛtāH//

2.60a: krānteH kramotkrammajye dve kṛtvā tatrotkramajyayā/
2.60b: hīnā trijyā dinavyāsadalaṃ taddakṣiṇottaram//

2.61a: krāntijyā viṣuvadbhāghnī kṣitijyā dvādaśoddhṛtā/
2.61b: trijyāguṇāhorātrārdhakarṇāptā carajāsavaH//

2.62a: tatkārmukam udakkrāntau *dhanaśanī pṛthakṣthite/(C dhanahānī)
2.62b: svāhorātracaturbhāge dinarātridale smṛte//

2.63a: yāmyakrāntau viparyaste dviguṇe tu dinakṣape/
2.63b: vikṣepayuktonitayā krāntyā bhānām api svake//

2.64a: bhabhogo +aṣṭaśatīliptāH khāśviśailās tathā titheH/
2.64b: grahaliptābhabhogāptā bhāni bhuktyā dinādikam//

2.65a: ravīnduyogaliptābhyo yogā bhabhogabhājitāH/
2.65b: gatā gamyāś ca ṣaṣṭighnyo bhuktiyogāptanāḍikāH//

2.66a: arkonacandraliptābhyas tithayo bhogabhājitāH/
2.66b: gatā gamyāś ca ṣaṣṭighnyo nāḍyo bhuktyantaroddhṛtāH//

2.67a: dhruvāṇi śakunir nāgaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu catuṣpadam/
2.67b: kiṃstughnaṃ tu caturdaśyāH kṛṣṇāyāś cāparārdhataH//

2.68a: bavādīni tataH sapta carākhyakaraṇāni ca/
2.68b: māse +aṣṭakṛtva ekaikaṃ karaṇānāṃ pravartate//

2.69a: tithyardhabhogaṃ sarveṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ prakalpayet/
2.69b: eṣā sphutagatiH proktā sūryādīnāṃ khacāriṇām//

3.01a: śilātale +ambusaṃśuddhe vajralepe +api vā same/
3.01b: tatra śaṅkvaṅgulair iṣṭaiH samaṃ maṇḍalam ālikhet//

3.02a: tanmadhye sthāpayec chaṅkuṃ kalpanādvādaśāṅgulam/
3.02b: tacchāyāgraṃ spṛśed yatra vṛtte pūrvāparārdhayoH//

3.03a: tatra bindū vidhāyobhau vṛtte pūrvāparābhidhau/
3.03b: tanmadhye timinā rekhā kartavyā dakṣiṇottarā//

3.04a: yāmyottaradiśor madhye timinā pūrvapaścimā/
3.04b: diṅmadhyamatsyaiH saṃsādhyā vidiśas tadvad eva hi//

3.05a: caturasraṃ bahiH kuryāt sūtrair madhyād vinirgataiH/
3.05b: bhujasūtrāṅgulais tatra dattair iṣṭaprabhā smṛtā//

3.06a: prākpaścimāśritā rekhā procyate samamaṇḍale/
3.06b: unaṇḍale ca viṣuvanmaṇḍale parikīrtyate//

3.07a: rekhā prācyaparā sādhyā viṣuvadbhāgragā tathā/
3.07b: iṣṭacchāyāviṣuvator madhyam agrābhidhīyate//

3.08a: śaṅkucchāyākṛtiyuter mūlaṃ karṇo +asya vargataH/
3.08b: projjhya śaṅkukṛtiṃ mūlaṃ chāyā śaṅkur viparyayāt//

3.09a: triṃśatkṛtyo yuge bhānāṃ cakraṃ prāk parilambate/
3.09b: tadguṇād bhūdinair bhaktād dyugaṇād yad avāpyate//

3.10a: taddos trighnā daśāptāṃśā vijñeyā ayanābhidhāH/
3.10b: tatsaṃskṛtād grahāt krānticchāyācaradalādikam//

3.11a: sphuṭaṃ dṛktulyatāṃ gacched ayane viṣuvadvaye/
3.11b: prāk cakraṃ calitaṃ hīne chāyārkāt karaṇāgate//

3.12a: antarāṃśair athāvṛtya paścāc cheṣais tathādhike/
3.12b: evaṃ viṣuvatī chāyā svadeśe yā dinārdhajā//
3.13a: dakṣiṇottararekhāyāṃ sā tatra viṣuvatprabhā//
3.13b: śaṅkucchāyāhate trijye viṣuvatkarṇabhājite/

3.14a: lambākṣajye tayoś cāpe lambākṣau dakṣiṇau sadā/
3.14b: madhyacchāyā bhujas tena guṇitā tribhamaurvikā//

3.15a: svakarṇāptā dhanurliptā natās tā dakṣiṇe bhuje/
3.15b: uttarāś cottare yāmyās tāH sūryakrāntiliptikāH//
body.translated_text: [3.15] The arc-minutes of the bow [declination], obtained by one's own hypotenuse, when south are in the south arm; those that are north are in the north — these are the arc-minutes of the sun's declination (<s>krānti</s>).

body.text:
3.16a: digbhede miśritāH sāmye viśliṣṭāś cākṣaliptikāH/
3.16b: tābhyo +akṣajyā ca tadvargaṃ projjhya trijyākṛteH padam//
body.translated_text: [3.16] When the directions differ, they are combined; when the same, they are separated — these are the arc-minutes of the latitude (<s>akṣa</s>). From these, the latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>); and subtracting its square from the square of the radius (<s>trijyā</s>), [take] the root.

body.text:
3.17a: lambajyārkaguṇākṣajyā viṣuvadbhātha lambayā/
3.17b: svākṣārkanatabhāgānāṃ dikṣāmye +antaram anyathā//
body.translated_text: [3.17] The co-latitude sine (<s>lambajyā</s>) [equals] the sun's sine multiplied by the latitude-sine. Then, from the equinoctial shadow by the co-latitude: the difference of one's latitude and the sun's declination degrees when the directions are the same; otherwise [the sum].

body.text:
3.18a: digbhede +apakramaH śeṣas tasya jyā trijyayā hatā/
3.18b: paramāpakramajyāptā cāpaṃ meṣādigo raviH//
body.translated_text: [3.18] When the directions differ, the remainder is the declination (<s>apakrama</s>). Its sine, multiplied by the radius, divided by the maximum declination-sine — the arc [gives] the sun [reckoned] from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> [Aries].

body.text:
3.19a: karkyādau projjhya cakrārdhāt tulādau bhārdhasaṃyutāt/
3.19b: mṛgādau projjhya bhagaṇān madhyāhne +arkaH sphuṭo bhavet//
body.translated_text: [3.19] Beginning from <s>Karka</s> [Cancer], subtract from the semicircle; from <s>Tulā</s> [Libra], add half the circle; from <s>Mṛga</s> [Capricorn], subtract the full revolutions — at midday the sun becomes true (<s>sphuṭa</s>).

body.text:
3.20a: tanmāndam asakṛd vāmaṃ phalaṃ madhyo divākaraH/
3.20b: svākṣārkāpakramayutir dikṣāmye +antaram anyathā//
body.translated_text: [3.20] Its equation of center (<s>manda</s>), repeatedly [applied], the result to the left, [gives] the mean sun. The sum of one's latitude and the sun's declination when the directions are the same; the difference otherwise.

body.text:
3.21a: śeṣaṃ natāṃśāH sūryasya tadbāhujyā ca koṭijyā/
3.21b: śaṅkumānāṅgulābhyaste bhujatrijye yathākramam//
body.translated_text: [3.21] The remainder is the sun's degrees of zenith distance (<s>nata</s>). Its base-sine (<s>bāhujyā</s>) and perpendicular-sine (<s>koṭijyā</s>), multiplied by the gnomon-measure in <s>aṅgulas</s>, [equal] the base and radius respectively.

body.text:
3.22a: koṭijyayā vibhajyāpte chāyākarṇāv ahardale/
3.22b: krāntijyā viṣuvatkarṇaguṇāptā śaṅkujīvayā//
body.translated_text: [3.22] Dividing by the perpendicular-sine, one obtains the shadow and the shadow-hypotenuse at half the day. The declination-sine multiplied by the equinoctial hypotenuse, divided by the gnomon-sine,

body.text:
3.23a: arkāgrā sveṣṭakarṇaghnī madhyakarṇoddhṛtā svakā/
3.23b: viṣuvadbhāyutārkāgrā yāmye syād uttaro bhujaH//
body.translated_text: [3.23] [gives] the sun's amplitude (<s>arkāgrā</s>). [This], multiplied by one's chosen hypotenuse and divided by the midday hypotenuse, [gives] one's own [amplitude]. The equinoctial shadow added to the amplitude: when south, the base is north.

body.text:
3.24a: viṣuvatyām viśodhyodaggole syād bāhur uttaraH/
3.24b: viparyayād bhujo yāmyo bhavet prācyaparāntare//
body.translated_text: [3.24] At the equinox, when the [amplitude] is subtracted in the northern hemisphere, the base is north; when reversed, the base is south — between east and west.

body.text:
3.25a: mādhyāhniko bhujo nityaṃ chāyā mādhyāhnikī smṛtā/
3.25b: lambākṣajīve viṣuvacchāyādvādaśasaṅguṇe//
body.translated_text: [3.25] The midday base is always the midday shadow. The co-latitude and latitude sines [are derived from] the equinoctial shadow multiplied by twelve.

body.text:
3.26a: krāntijyāpte tu tau karṇau samamaṇḍalage ravau/
3.26b: saumyākṣonā yadā kāntiH syāt tadā dyudalaśravaH//
body.translated_text: [3.26] Divided by the declination-sine, those two are the hypotenuses when the sun is on the prime vertical. When the north declination is less than the latitude, then there is a half-day hypotenuse.

body.text:
3.27a: viṣuvacchāyayābhyastaH karṇo madhyāgrayoddhṛtaH/
3.27b: svakrāntijyā trijīvāghnī lambajyāptāgramaurvikā//
body.translated_text: [3.27] The equinoctial shadow multiplied by the hypotenuse, divided by the midday amplitude; one's declination-sine multiplied by the radius and divided by the co-latitude-sine [gives] the amplitude base.

body.text:
3.28a: sveṣṭakarṇahatā bhaktā trijyayāgrāṅgulādikā/
3.28b: trijyāvargārdhato +agrajyāvargonād dvādaśāhatāt//
body.translated_text: [3.28] [The amplitude], multiplied by one's chosen hypotenuse and divided by the radius, [gives] the amplitude in <s>aṅgulas</s> etc. From [the square of] half the square of the radius, minus the square of the amplitude-sine, multiplied by twelve,

body.text:
3.29a: punar dvādaśanighnāc ca labhyate yat phalaṃ budhaiH/
3.29b: śaṅkuvargārdhasaṃyuktaviṣuvadvargabhājitāt//
body.translated_text: [3.29] and again multiplied by twelve, what the learned obtain as the result — divided by the sum of half the gnomon-square and the equinoctial square —

body.text:
3.30a: tadeva karaṇī nāma tāṃ pṛthak sthāpayed budhaH/
3.30b: arkaghnī viṣuvacchāyāgrajyayā guṇitā tathā//
body.translated_text: [3.30] that itself is called the 'producer' (<s>karaṇī</s>). The learned should set it aside separately. Multiplied by the sun and multiplied by the equinoctial shadow's amplitude-sine,

body.text:
3.31a: bhaktā phalākhyaṃ tadvargasaṃyuktakaraṇīpadam/
3.31b: phalena hīnasaṃyuktaṃ dakṣiṇottaragolayoH//
body.translated_text: [3.31] divided, the result [is obtained]; the root of the sum of its square and the 'producer' — diminished or increased by the result, for the southern and northern hemispheres.

body.text:
3.32a: yāmyayor vidiśoH śaṅkur evaṃ yāmyottare ravau/
3.32b: paribhramati śaṅkos tu śaṅkur uttarayos tu saH//
body.translated_text: [3.32] In the two southern intermediate directions, the gnomon [is computed] thus, when the sun is south or north. The gnomon revolves, but the gnomon [itself] is for the northern [positions].

body.text:
3.33a: tattrijyāvargaviśleṣān mūlaṃ dṛgjyābhidhīyate/
3.33b: svaśaṅkunā vibhajyāpte dṛktrijye dvādaśāhate//
body.translated_text: [3.33] The root of the difference of its [square] and the square of the radius is called the sight-sine (<s>dṛgjyā</s>). Divided by one's gnomon, the sight-radii obtained, multiplied by twelve,

body.text:
3.34a: chāyākarṇau tu koṇeṣu yathāsvaṃ deśakālayoH/
3.34b: trijyodakcarajāyuktā yāmyāyāṃ tadvivarjitā//
body.translated_text: [3.34] [give] the shadow and hypotenuse in the intermediate directions, each according to its place and time. The radius plus the day-arc [value] when south; minus that when [north].

body.text:
3.35a: antyā natotkramajyonā svahorātrārdhasaṅguṇā/
3.35b: trijyābhaktā bhavec chedo lambajyāghno +atha bhājitaH//
body.translated_text: [3.35] The final versed sine diminished by the zenith distance versed sine, multiplied by half of one's day-arc, divided by the radius, gives the intercept (<s>cheda</s>). Multiplied by the co-latitude sine and divided

body.text:
3.36a: tribhajyayā bhavec chaṅkus tadvargaṃ pariśodhayet/
3.36b: trijyāvargāt padaṃ dṛgjyā chāyākarṇau tu pūrvavat//
body.translated_text: [3.36] by the radius, gives the gnomon. Subtract its square from the square of the radius; the root [is] the sight-sine. Shadow and hypotenuse as before.

body.text:
3.37a: abhīṣṭacchāyayābhyastā trijyā tatkarṇabhājitā/
3.37b: dṛgjyā tadvargasaṃśuddhāt trijyāvargāc ca yat padam/
body.translated_text: [3.37] The desired shadow multiplied by the radius, divided by its hypotenuse, [gives] the sight-sine. The root of the difference of its square from the square of the radius —

body.text:
3.38a: śaṅkuH sa tribhajīvāghnaH svalambajyāvibhājitaH/
3.38b: chedaH sa trijyayābhyastaH svāhorātrārdhabhājitaH//
body.translated_text: [3.38] [is] the gnomon. That multiplied by the radius, divided by one's co-latitude sine, [gives] the intercept. That multiplied by the radius, divided by half one's day-arc —

body.text:
3.39a: unnatajyā tayā hīnā svāntyā śeṣasya kārmukam/
3.39b: utkramajyābhir evaṃ syuH prākpaścārdhanatāsavaH//
body.translated_text: [3.39] [gives] the altitude-sine (<s>unnatajyā</s>). The final [value] diminished by it — the arc of the remainder — through the versed sines, thus are obtained the east and west half-arc ascensions (<s>nata</s>).

body.text:
3.40a: iṣṭāgrāghnī tu lambajyā svakarṇāṅgulabhājitā/
3.40b: krāntijyā sā trijīvāghnī paramāpakramoddhṛtā//
body.translated_text: [3.40] The desired amplitude multiplied by the co-latitude sine, divided by one's hypotenuse in <s>aṅgulas</s>, [gives] the declination-sine. That multiplied by the radius, divided by the maximum declination,

body.text:
3.41a: taccāpaṃ bhādikaṃ kṣetraṃ padais tatra bhavo raviH/
3.41b: iṣṭe +ahni madhye prākpaścād dhṛte bāhutrayāntare//
body.translated_text: [3.41] its arc in degrees etc. [gives] the longitude; there the sun exists. On the desired day, at midday, east and west, within the three-base interval,

body.text:
3.42a: matsyadvayāntarayutes trispṛkṣūtreṇa bhābhramaH/
3.42b: tribhadyukarṇārdhaguṇāH svāhorātrārdhabhājitāH//
body.translated_text: [3.42] the revolution of the [zodiacal] signs [is found] by a thread touching three [points] between two fish-figures. [The values] multiplied by half the day-hypotenuse for three [signs], divided by half one's day-arc,

body.text:
3.43a: kramād ekadvitribhajyās taccāpāni pṛthak pṛthak/
3.43b: svādho +adhaH pariśodhyātha meṣāl laṅkodayāsavaH//
body.translated_text: [3.43] give sequentially the one-, two-, and three-sign sines. Their arcs, each separately, subtracted successively below, [give] from <s>Meṣa</s> the rising [arcs] at <s>Laṅkā</s>.

body.text:
3.44a: khāgāṣṭayo +arthago +agaikāH śaratryaṅkahimāṃśavaH/
3.44b: svadeśacarakhaṇḍonā bhavantīṣṭodayāsavaH//
body.translated_text: [3.44] [The values are:] 1670, 1795, 1935 [for the first three signs]. Diminished by the local ascensional differences, they become the desired rising arcs.

body.text:
3.45a: vyastā vyastair yutāH svaiH svaiH karkaṭādyās tatas trayaH/
3.45b: utkrameṇa ṣaḍevaite bhavantīṣṭās tulādayaH//
body.translated_text: [3.45] The reverse [signs], with their own [values] reversed, — the three beginning from <s>Karkaṭa</s> [Cancer]; in reverse order, these same six become the desired [arcs] from <s>Tulā</s> [Libra] onward.

body.text:
3.46a: gatabhogyāsavaH kāryā bhāskarād iṣṭakālikāt/
3.46b: svodayāsuhatā bhuktabhogyā bhaktāH khavahnibhiH//
body.translated_text: [3.46] The elapsed and remaining arcs should be computed from the sun at the desired time. [The arc] multiplied by its own rising arc, the elapsed and remaining [portions] divided by 360.

body.text:
3.47a: abhīṣṭaghaṭikāsubhyo bhogyāsūn praviśodhayet/
3.47b: tadvat tadeṣyalagnāsūn evaṃ yātāt tathotkramāt//
body.translated_text: [3.47] From the desired <s>ghaṭikā</s>-arcs, subtract the remaining arcs. Likewise [subtract] the sought <s>lagna</s> arcs. Thus from the elapsed, in reverse order.

body.text:
3.48a: śeṣaṃ cet triṃśatābhyastam aśuddhena vibhājitam/
3.48b: bhāgair yuktaṃ ca hīnaṃ ca tallagnaṃ kṣitije tadā// (C bhāgahīnaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca)
body.translated_text: [3.48] If there is a remainder, multiplied by thirty and divided by the unexhausted [arc], added to or subtracted from degrees — that is the <s>lagna</s> on the horizon at that time.

body.text:
3.49a: prākpaścān natanāḍībhis tasmāl laṅkodayāsubhiH/
3.49b: bhānau kṣayadhane kṛtvā madhyalagnaṃ tadā bhavet//
body.translated_text: [3.49] From the east and west arc-<s>nāḍīs</s>, by the <s>Laṅkā</s> rising arcs, applying decrease and increase to the sun, the mid-heaven <s>lagna</s> is then obtained.

body.text:
3.50a: bhogyāsūn ūnakasyātha bhuktāsūn adhikasya ca/
3.50b: sampīṇḍyāntaralagnāsūn evaṃ syāt kālasādhanam//
body.translated_text: [3.50] [Adding] the remaining arcs of the lesser and the elapsed arcs of the greater, combining the interval <s>lagna</s> arcs — thus the determination of time is achieved.

body.text:
3.51a: sūryād ūne niśāśeṣe lagne +arkād adhike divā/
3.51b: bhacakrārdhayutād bhānor adhikke +astamayāt param//
body.translated_text: [3.51] When the <s>lagna</s> is less than the sun, it is the remainder of the night. When greater than the sun, it is daytime. When greater than the sun plus half the zodiac, it is after sunset.

body.text:
[candragrahaṇa]
4.01a: sārdhāni ṣaṭsahasrāṇi yojanāni vivasvataH/
4.01b: viṣkambho maṇḍalasyendoH sahāśītyā catuśśatam//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on Lunar Eclipses] [4.01] Six thousand and a half <s>yojanas</s> is the diameter of the sun's orb. The moon's orb is four hundred and eighty [<s>yojanas</s>].

body.text:
4.02a: sphuṭasvabhuktyā guṇitau madhyabhuktyoddhṛtau sphuṭau/
4.02b: raveH svabhagaṇābhyastaH śaśāṅkabhagaṇoddhṛtaH//
body.translated_text: [4.02] [The diameters], multiplied by the true daily motion and divided by the mean daily motion, become true. [The sun's], multiplied by its own revolutions and divided by the moon's revolutions,

body.text:
4.03a: śaśāṅkakakṣāguṇito bhājito vā +arkakakṣayā/
4.03b: viṣkambhaś candrakakṣāyāṃ tithyāptā mānaliptikā//
body.translated_text: [4.03] or multiplied by the moon's orbit and divided by the sun's orbit — [gives] the diameter in the moon's orbit. [This], divided by the <s>tithi</s> [gives] the arc-minutes of measure.

body.text:
4.04a: sphuṭendubhuktir bhūvyāsaguṇitā madhyayoddhṛtā/
4.04b: labdhaṃ sūcī mahīvyāsasphuṭārkaśravaṇāntaram//
body.translated_text: [4.04] The true lunar daily motion multiplied by the earth's diameter and divided by the mean [motion] — the result is the shadow-cone (<s>sūcī</s>). [This is] the interval between the earth's diameter and the sun's true hypotenuse.

body.text:
4.05a: madhyenduvyāsaguṇitaṃ madhyārkavyāsabhājitam/
4.05b: viśodhya labdhaṃ sūcyāṃ tu tamo liptās tu pūrvavat//
body.translated_text: [4.05] [The earth's diameter], multiplied by the mean lunar diameter and divided by the mean solar diameter — subtracting the result from the cone — the shadow [diameter] in arc-minutes is as before.

body.text:
4.06a: bhānor bhārdhe mahīcchāyā tattulye +arkasame +api/
4.06b: śaśāṅkapāte grahaṇaṃ kiyadbhāgādhikonake//
body.translated_text: [4.06] In half a [zodiacal] sign from the sun, the earth's shadow — when equal to the sun. When the moon's node is within a certain degree [of the sun], an eclipse [occurs].

body.text:
4.07a: tulyau rāśyādibhiH syātām amāvāsyāntakālikau/
4.07b: sūryendū paurṇamāsyante bhārdhe bhāgādikau samau//
body.translated_text: [4.07] [The sun and moon] should be equal in signs, degrees, etc. at the end of the new moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>). At the end of the full moon (<s>paurṇamāsī</s>), equal in half-sign degrees etc.

body.text:
4.08a: gataiṣyaparvanāḍīnāṃ svaphalenonasaṃyutau/
4.08b: samaliptau bhavetāṃ tau pātas tātkāliko +anyathā//
body.translated_text: [4.08] The elapsed and future <s>parvan</s>-<s>nāḍīs</s>, diminished or increased by their own result, when the arc-minutes become equal, those two are the contemporary node; otherwise [not].

body.text:
4.09a: chādako bhāskarasyendur adhaHstho ghanavad bhavet/
4.09b: bhūcchāyāṃ prāṅmukhaś candro viśaty asya bhaved asau//
body.translated_text: [4.09] The moon, being below [the sun], obscures the sun like a solid body. The moon, moving eastward, enters the earth's shadow — this [lunar eclipse] occurs.

body.text:
4.10a: tātkālikenduvikṣepaṃ chādyacchādakamānayoH/
4.10b: yogārdhāt projjhya yaccheṣaṃ tāvac channaṃ tad ucyate//
body.translated_text: [4.10] The contemporary lunar latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>), [subtracted] from half the sum of the diameters of the eclipsed and eclipsing bodies — whatever remains, that much is said to be obscured.

body.text:
4.11a: yad grāhyam adhike tasmin sakalaṃ nyūnam anyathā/
4.11b: yogārdhād adhike na syād vikṣepe grāsasambhavaH//
body.translated_text: [4.11] What is to be eclipsed: when greater, [the eclipse is] total; when less, otherwise. When the latitude exceeds half the sum, there is no occurrence of an eclipse.

body.text:
4.12a: grāhyagrāhakasaṃyogaviyogau dalitau pṛthak/
4.12b: vikṣepavargahīnābhyāṃ tadvargābhyām ubhe pade//
body.translated_text: [4.12] The conjunction and separation of eclipsed and eclipsing [bodies], each halved separately, [provide] the roots of the two [values] diminished by the square of the latitude from those squares.

body.text:
4.13a: ṣaṣṭhyā saṃguṇya sūryendvor bhuktyantaravibhājite/
4.13b: syātāṃ sthitivimardārdhe nāḍikādiphale tayoH//
body.translated_text: [4.13] Multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference of the daily motions of the sun and moon — these become the half-durations of immersion (<s>sthiti</s>) and totality (<s>vimarda</s>), in <s>nāḍikās</s> etc.

body.text:
4.14a: sthityardhanāḍikābhyastā gatayaH ṣaṣṭhibhājitāH/
4.14b: liptādi pragrahe śodhyaṃ mokṣe deyaṃ punaH punaH//
body.translated_text: [4.14] The daily motions multiplied by the half-duration <s>nāḍikās</s> and divided by sixty — the arc-minutes etc. [result]. At first contact (<s>pragraha</s>), subtract; at release (<s>mokṣa</s>), add repeatedly.

body.text:
4.15a: tadvikṣepaiH sthitidalaṃ vimardārdhe tathā +asakṛt/
4.15b: saṃsādhyam anyathā pāte talliptādiphalaṃ svakam//
body.translated_text: [4.15] With the [corrected] latitudes, the half-duration and half-totality should be repeatedly refined. Otherwise, at the node, the result in arc-minutes etc. is its own.

body.text:
4.16a: sphuṭatithyavasāne tu madhyagrahaṇam ādiśet/
4.16b: sthityardhanāḍikāhīne grāso mokṣas tu saṃyute//
body.translated_text: [4.16] At the end of the true <s>tithi</s>, one should predict the mid-eclipse. Diminished by the half-duration <s>nāḍikās</s>, [gives] first contact; increased, [gives] release.

body.text:
4.17a: tadvad eva vimardārdhanāḍikāhīnasaṃyute/
4.17b: nimīlanonmīlanākhye bhavetāṃ sakalagrahe//
body.translated_text: [4.17] Likewise, diminished and increased by the half-totality <s>nāḍikās</s> — the so-called immersion (<s>nimīlana</s>) and emersion (<s>unmīlana</s>) occur in a total eclipse.

body.text:
4.18a: iṣṭanāḍīvihīnena sthityardhenārkacandrayoH/
4.18b: bhuktyantaraṃ samāhanyāt ṣaṣṭyāptāH koṭiliptikāH//
body.translated_text: From the half-duration [of the eclipse] diminished by the desired <s>nāḍīs</s>, multiply the difference of daily motions of the Sun and Moon; dividing by sixty gives the perpendicular-minutes (<s>koṭiliptā</s>). //

body.text:
4.19a: bhānor grahe koṭiliptā madhyasthityardhasaṃguṇāH/
4.19b: sphuṭasthityardhasaṃbhaktāH sphuṭāH koṭikalāH smṛtā//
body.translated_text: In a solar eclipse, the perpendicular-minutes multiplied by the mean half-duration and divided by the true half-duration are the true perpendicular-minutes. //

body.text:
4.20a: kṣepo bhujas tayor vargayuter mūlaṃ śravas tu tat/
4.20b: mānayogārdhataH projjhya grāsas tātkāliko bhavet//
body.translated_text: The latitude is the base (<s>bhuja</s>); the square root of the sum of the squares of those two is the hypotenuse. Subtracting from half the sum of the [apparent] diameters gives the obscuration at that instant. //

body.text:
4.21a: madhyagrahaṇataś cordhvam iṣṭanāḍīr viśodhayet/
4.21b: sthityardhān maukṣikāc cheṣaṃ prāgvac ccheṣaṃ tu maukṣike//
body.translated_text: From the mid-eclipse [time], subtract the desired <s>nāḍīs</s> upward; subtract from the half-duration of the release-phase; the remainder [is treated] as before, and the remainder is in the release [phase]. //

body.text:
4.22a: grāhyagrāhakayogārdhāc chodhyāH svacchannaliptikāH/
4.22b: tādvargāt projjhya tatkālavikṣepasya kṛtiṃ padam//
body.translated_text: Subtract the obscured arc-minutes from half the sum of [the diameters of] the eclipsed and the eclipser. From the square of that, subtract the square of the current latitude — [take] the square root. //

body.text:
4.23a: koṭiliptā raveH spaṣṭasthityardhenāhatā hṛtāH/
4.23b: madhyena liptās tannāḍyaH sthitivad grāsanāḍikāH//
body.translated_text: The perpendicular-minutes of the Sun, multiplied by the true half-duration and divided by the mean [half-duration], give the arc-minutes; those <s>nāḍīs</s> are the obscuration-<s>nāḍīs</s>, [computed] like the half-duration. //

body.text:
4.24a: natajyā +akṣajyayābhyastā trijyāptā tasya kārmukam/
4.24b: valanāṃśā saumyayāmyāH pūrvāparakapālayoH//
body.translated_text: The sine of the hour angle (<s>natajyā</s>), multiplied by the sine of the latitude (<s>akṣajyā</s>) and divided by the radius, gives its arc. The degrees of deflection (<s>valana</s>) are north or south, in the eastern and western hemispheres [respectively]. //

body.text:
4.25a: rāśitrayayutād grāhyāt krāntyaṃśair dikṣamair yutāH/
4.25b: bhede +antarāj jyā valanā saptatyaṅgulabhājitā//
body.translated_text: From the eclipsed [body] increased by three signs, the deflection in declination-degrees with the same direction — when different, [take] the sine of the difference. The deflection [is obtained by] dividing by seventy <s>aṅgulas</s>. //

body.text:
4.26a: sonnataṃ dinamadhyārdhaṃ dinārdhāptaṃ phalena tu/
4.26b: chindyād vikṣepamānāni tāny eṣām aṅgulāni tu//
body.translated_text: Half the day [duration] increased by the hour angle, divided by [that same] half-day, multiplied by the result — this cuts the eclipse magnitude measures; these are their <s>aṅgula</s> values. //

body.text:
[sūryagrahaṇa]
5.01a: madhyalagnasame bhānau harijasya na sambhavaH/
5.01b: akṣodaṅmadhyabhakrāntisāmye nāvanater api//
body.translated_text: [Solar Eclipse:] When the Sun is at the mid-heaven ascendant (<s>madhyalagnasama</s>), there is no solar eclipse. [Also] when the latitude of the location equals the declination of the mid-heaven, there is no parallax in altitude (<s>avanati</s>). //

body.text:
5.02a: deśakālaviśeṣeṇa yathāvanatisambhavaH/
5.02b: lambanasyāpi pūrvānyadigvaśāc ca tathocyate//
body.translated_text: Due to the particularity of place and time, as parallax in altitude arises, so too parallax in longitude (<s>lambana</s>) arises due to the eastern and western directions — thus it is stated. //

body.text:
5.03a: lagnaṃ parvāntanāḍīnāṃ kuryāt svair udayāsubhiH/
5.03b: tajjyāntyāpakramajyāghnī lambajyāptodayābhidhā//
body.translated_text: One should compute the ascendant (<s>lagna</s>) for the <s>nāḍīs</s> at the end of the <s>parvan</s> using the rising times for one's own [latitude]. The sine of the end [of the ascendant sign], multiplied by the sine of the declination and divided by the cosine of the latitude, gives the rising [time]. //

body.text:
5.04a: tadā laṅkodayair lagnaṃ madhyasaṃjñaṃ yathoditam/
5.04b: tatkrāntyakṣāṃśasaṃyogo dikṣāmye +antaram anyathā//
body.translated_text: Then the ascendant computed with the <s>Laṅkā</s> rising times is called the mean [ascendant], as stated. The combination of its declination and the latitude-degrees — when of the same direction, [take the] sum; otherwise, the difference. //

body.text:
5.05a: śeṣaṃ natāṃśās tanmaurvī madhyajyā sābhidhīyate/
5.05b: madhyodayajyayābhyastā trijyāptā vargitaṃ phalam//
body.translated_text: The remainder is the zenith-distance degrees (<s>natāṃśa</s>); the sine of that is called the mid-sine (<s>madhyajyā</s>). Multiplied by the rising-sine and divided by the radius, the result is squared. //

body.text:
5.06a: madhyajyāvargaviśliṣṭaṃ dṛkkṣepaH śeṣataH padam/
5.06b: tattrijyāvargaviśleṣān mūlaṃ śaṅkuH sa dṛggatiH//
body.translated_text: From the square of the mid-sine, subtract [that product]; the square root of the remainder is the parallax in latitude (<s>dṛkkṣepa</s>). From the square of the radius minus the square of that, the root is the gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>), [also called] the dṛggati. //

body.text:
5.07a: natāṃśabāhukoṭijye +asphuṭe dṛkkṣepadṛggatī/
5.07b: ekajyārdhagataś chedo labdhaṃ dṛggatijīvayā//
body.translated_text: When the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> is greater than the sum of the half-diameters of the Sun and Moon, no solar eclipse occurs, even at the end of the new-moon day. //

body.text:
5.08a: madhyalagnārkaviśleṣajyā chedena vibhājitā/
5.08b: ravīndvor lambanaṃ jñeyaṃ prākpaścād ghaṭikādikam//
body.translated_text: From the gnomon, the sine of the parallax in longitude (<s>lambana</s>) — that divided by the radius gives the <s>nāḍīs</s> of the parallax. //

body.text:
5.09a: madhyalagnādhike bhānau tithyantāt praviśodhayet/
5.09b: dhanam ūne +asakṛt karma yāvat sarvaṃ sthirībhavet//
body.translated_text: The parallax <s>nāḍīs</s> multiplied by the difference of daily motions and divided by sixty give the parallax in arc-minutes. Applied to the mean conjunction [time], [it gives] the true conjunction. //

body.text:
5.10a: dṛkkṣepaH śītatigmāṃśvor madhyabhuktyantarāhataH/
5.10b: tithighnatrijyayā bhakto labdhaṃ sāvanatir bhavet//
body.translated_text: Iterating this again yields the corrected [result]; from the resulting conjunction, [compute] the half-duration and so forth as before. //

body.text:
5.11a: dṛkkṣepāt saptatihṛtād bhaved vāvanatiH phalam/
5.11b: athavā trijyayā bhaktāt saptasaptakasaṅguṇāt//
body.translated_text: As stated previously for the lunar eclipse, the half-duration [is computed] from the [modified] half-sum of diameters; the half-duration of totality [is computed] from the half-difference of diameters. //

body.text:
5.12a: madhyajyādigvaśāt sā ca vijñeyā dakṣiṇottarā/
5.12b: senduvikṣepadikṣāmye yuktā viśleṣitānyathā//
body.translated_text: In the solar eclipse, the eclipser is the Moon; in the lunar, the shadow. The Moon's latitude is the latitude in both cases, computed as previously stated. //

body.text:
5.13a: tayā sthitivimardārdhagrāsādyaṃ tu yathoditam/
5.13b: pramāṇaṃ valanābhīṣṭagrāsādi himaraśmivat//
body.translated_text: Since the Moon is near and the Sun far, the Moon covers the Sun; the shadow, being far, [covers] the Moon. Since the sizes [of the eclipsers] differ, the obscuration amounts are different. //

body.text:
5.14a: sthityardhonādhikāt prāgvat tithyā(?)ntalāl lambanaṃ punaH/
5.14b: grāsamokṣodbhavaṃ sādhyaṃ tanmadhyaharijāntaram//
body.translated_text: The moon's disk-diameter is the diameter of the eclipser in a solar eclipse. Therefore, in a solar eclipse, the computation differs from the lunar eclipse. //

body.text:
5.15a: prākkapāle +adhikaṃ madhyād bhavet prāgrahaṇaṃ yadi/
5.15b: maukṣikaṃ lambanaṃ hīnaṃ paścārdhe tu viparyayaH//
body.translated_text: One should compute the obscuration, deflection, color, and the [eclipse] diagram as before, [but] using the Sun's disk and the parallax-corrected latitude. //

body.text:
5.16a: tadā mokṣasthitidale deyaṃ pragrahaṇe tathā/
5.16b: harijāntarakaṃ śodhyaṃ yatraitat syād viparyayaH//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on Projection (<s>Yantraprakaraṇa</s>):] On a flat surface or a sphere, having drawn the ecliptic path according to direction and the path of the eclipsed body, //

body.text:
5.17a: etad uktaṃ kapālaikye tadbhede lambanaikatā/
5.17b: sve sve sthitidale yojyā vimardārdhe +api coktavat//
body.translated_text: the point of intersection of those two [paths] and the path of the eclipser — their meeting, beginning from the east, should be shown by one who knows the directions. //

body.text:
[chedyaka]
6.01a: na chedyakam ṛte yasmād bhedā grahaṇayoH sphuṭāH/
6.01b: jñāyante tat pravakṣyāmi chedyakajñānam uttamam//
body.translated_text: From the mid-eclipse [time], the measure of the hypotenuse [placed] in the direction of deflection — the center of the eclipser is there; draw [the eclipser's disk] with its own half-diameter. //

body.text:
6.02a: susādhitāyām avanau binduṃ kṛtvā tato likhet/
6.02b: saptavargāṅgulenādau maṇḍalaṃ valanāśritam//
body.translated_text: What is covered of the eclipsed [body's] disk — that region, enclosed by the two arcs, is the [visible] obscuration. //

body.text:
6.03a: grāhyagrāhakayogārdhasammitena dvitīyakam/
6.03b: maṇḍalaṃ tat samāsākhyaṃ grāhyārdhena tṛtīyakam//
body.translated_text: The color of the eclipsed Moon: at the beginning, smoke-colored; when half-obscured, dark; during totality, tawny; at [the time of] greatest obscuration, coppery; at release, smoke-colored and then white. //

body.text:
6.04a: yāmyottarāprācyaparāsādhanaṃ pūrvavad diśām/
6.04b: prāg indor grahaṇaṃ paścān mokṣo +arkasya viparyayāt//
body.translated_text: In a solar eclipse, the color [determination] does not arise because the eclipser (Moon) is dense; the degrees of the Sun [visible as] a ring of light [during annular eclipse] should be known by the wise. //

body.text:
6.05a: yathādiśaṃ prāgrahaṇaṃ valanaṃ himadīdhiteH/
6.05b: maukṣikaṃ tu viparyastaṃ viparītam idaṃ raveH//
body.translated_text: At the beginning and end, the directions [of first and last contact]: in a lunar eclipse, [the shadow] strikes the Moon from the east; in a solar eclipse, [the Moon] strikes the Sun from the west. //

body.text:
6.06a: valanāgrān nayen madhyaṃ sūtraṃ yady atra saṃspṛśet/
6.06b: tatsamāse tato deyau vikṣepau grāsamaukṣikau//
body.translated_text: In a lunar eclipse, when the deflection (<s>valana</s>) and latitude are of the same direction, the first contact is in the opposite direction; when different, in the same direction. In a solar eclipse, the reverse. //

body.text:
6.07a: vikṣepāgrāt punaH sūtraṃ madhyabinduṃ praveśayet/
6.07b: tadgrāhyabindusaṃsparśād grāsamokṣau vinirdiśet//
body.translated_text: The release is reversed from that. Thus the first contact, greatest phase, and release are to be indicated in the directions of the deflection and latitude respectively. //

body.text:
6.08a: nityaśo +arkasya vikṣepāH parilekhe yathādiśam/
6.08b: viparītāH śaśāṅkasya tadvaśād atha madhyamam//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on Instruments:] I shall now explain the astronomical instruments for [computing] declination, shadow, ascensional difference, and so forth, as well as the observation of the planets. //

body.text:
6.09a: valanaṃ prāṅmukhaṃ deyaṃ tadvikṣepaikatā yadi/
6.09b: bhede paścān mukhaṃ deyam indor bhānor viparyayāt//
body.translated_text: Make a sphere (<s>gola</s>) of wood, uniform, smooth, and round; establish [on it] the two poles, the equator, and the ecliptic with the solstitial points. //

body.text:
6.10a: valanāgrāt punaH sūtraṃ madhyabinduṃ praveśayet/
6.10b: madhyasūtreṇa vikṣepaṃ valanābhimukhaṃ nayet//
body.translated_text: Place the [model] sun on the ecliptic at the appropriate degree; the shadows, rising times, and so forth will be seen [to correspond to observation]. //

body.text:
6.11a: vikṣepāgrāl likhed vṛttaṃ grāhakārdhena tena yat/
6.11b: grāhyavṛttaṃ samākrāntaṃ tadgrastaṃ tamasā bhavet//
body.translated_text: A water-clock (<s>ghaṭī</s>-instrument), a gnomon, a disk marked with degrees, a semicircle with a string [plumb-line] — these are the instruments for observing the heavens. //

body.text:
6.12a: chedyakaṃ likhatā bhūmau phalake vā vipaścitā/
6.12b: viparyayo diśāṃ kāryaH pūrvāparakapālayoH//
body.translated_text: At a distance from the sphere equal to the earth-sun distance [scaled down], fix a lamp; the sphere's own shadow [demonstrates eclipses]. //

body.text:
6.13a: svacchatvād dvādaśāṃśo +api grastaś candrasya dṛśyate/
6.13b: liptātrayam api grastaṃ tīkṣṇatvān na vivasvataH//
body.translated_text: When the shadow of the sphere falls on the [model] moon, that is a lunar eclipse; when the [model] moon's shadow falls on the sphere, that is a solar eclipse. //

body.text:
6.14a: svasaṃjñitās trayaH kāryā vikṣepāgreṣu bindavaH/
6.14b: tatra prāṅmadhyayor madhye tathā maukṣikamadhyayoH//
body.translated_text: Thus the god of the Sun has explained the established [methods of] the science of time (<s>kālajñāna</s>). //

body.text:
6.15a: likhen matsyau tayor madhyān mukhapucchaviniHsṛtam/
6.15b: prasārya sūtradvitayaṃ tayor yatra yutir bhavet//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on Cosmography:] The globe of the earth, formed of the five elements, dense, spherical, stands in the middle of space, in the center of the celestial sphere (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>). //

body.text:
6.16a: tatra sūtreṇa vilikhec cāpaṃ bindutrayaspṛśā/
6.16b: sa panthā grāhakasyoktā yenāsau samprayāsyati//
body.translated_text: Just as the round bulb of a <s>kadamba</s> flower is covered all around by blossoms, so the earth is surrounded on all sides by creatures. //

body.text:
6.17a: grāhyagrāhakayogārdhāt projjhyeṣṭagrāsam āgatam/
6.17b: avaśiṣṭāṅgulasamāṃ śalākāṃ madhyabindutaH//
body.translated_text: By the power of the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>), by the force of its own nature, it stands firm, unsupported, in the midst of the sky. //

body.text:
6.18a: tayor mārgonmukhīṃ dadyād grāsataH prāggrahāśritām/
6.18b: vimuñcato mokṣadiśi grāhakādhvānam eva sā//
body.translated_text: The city of the gods (<s>Devapura</s>) is in the east; to the south, <s>Saṃyamanī</s> (of <s>Yama</s>); the city of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> to the west; the city of the Moon to the north — [these are] on the equator. //

body.text:
6.19a: spṛśed yatra tato vṛttaṃ grāhakārdhena saṃlikhet/
6.19b: tena grāhyaṃ yadākrāntaṃ tat tamograstam ādiśet//
body.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Kumārī</s>, <s>Yamakoti</s>, and the city <s>Romaka</s> — these [places] are situated at the quadrants [of the equator], separated by a quarter of the circumference. //

body.text:
6.20a: mānāntarārdhena mitāṃ śalākāṃ grāsadiṅmukhīm/
6.20b: nimīlanākhyāṃ dadyāt sā tanmārge yatra saṃspṛśet//
body.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>, the golden mountain, stands at the north pole (<s>bhūmaddhya</s>); <s>Vadavāmukha</s> at the south. The gods see the Sun moving to the right; the <s>asuras</s> see it moving to the left. //

body.text:
6.21a: tato grāhakakhaṇḍena prāgvan maṇḍalam ālikhet/
6.21b: tadgrāhyamaṇḍalayutir yatra tatra nimīlanam//
body.translated_text: At <s>Meru</s>, [there is] sunrise when it is midday at <s>Laṅkā</s>, sunset in the west, and midnight in the city <s>Romaka</s>. //

body.text:
6.22a: evam unmīlane mokṣadiṅmukhīṃ samprasārayet/
6.22b: vilikhen maṇḍalaṃ prāgvad unmīlanam athoktavat//
body.translated_text: Those who are below [the equator] think 'we are above' just as those [above] do; for the sphere of the earth stands in space, and below and above depend on direction. //

body.text:
6.23a: ardhād ūne sadhūṃraṃ syāt kṛṣṇam ardhādhikaṃ bhavet/
6.23b: vimuñcataH kṛṣṇatāṃraṃ kapilaṃ sakalagrahe//
body.translated_text: The gods see the Sun after it has risen for half a year; the <s>asuras</s> [see it] for the other half. This is the day and night of the gods. //

body.text:
6.24a: rahasyam etad devānāṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit/
6.24b: suparīkṣitaśiṣyāya deyaṃ vatsaravāsine//
body.translated_text: This secret of the gods is not to be given to just anyone; it should be given to a well-tested student who has resided [with the teacher] for a year. //

body.text:
[grahayuti]
7.01a: tārāgrahāṇām anyonyaṃ syātāṃ yuddhasamāgamau/
7.01b: samāgamaH śaśāṅkena sūryeṇāstamanaṃ saha//
body.translated_text: [Chapter on Planetary Conjunctions:] Of the star-planets, conjunctions and encounters with each other [are called] conjunction (<s>samāgama</s>) and war (<s>yuddha</s>); [conjunction] with the Moon [is a meeting]; with the Sun, setting (<s>astamana</s>). //

body.text:
7.02a: śīghre mandādhike +atītaH saṃyogo bhavitānyathā/
7.02b: dvayoH prāgyāyinor evaṃ vakriṇos tu viparyayāt//
body.translated_text: When the <s>śīghra</s> [anomaly] exceeds the <s>manda</s>, the conjunction is past; otherwise, it is future. For two direct-moving [planets], this is so; for retrograde ones, the reverse. //

body.text:
7.03a: prāgyāyiny adhike +atīto vakriṇy eṣyaH samāgamaH/
7.03b: grahāntarakalāH svasvabhuktiliptāH samāhatāH//
body.translated_text: When the direct-moving one is greater [in longitude], the conjunction is past; when the retrograde [is greater], the conjunction is future. The arc-minutes of the difference between the planets, multiplied by their respective daily motions in minutes, //

body.text:
7.04a: bhuktyantareṇa vibhajed anulomavilomayoH/
7.04b: dvayor vakriṇy athaikasmin bhuktiyogena bhājayet//
body.translated_text: should be divided by the difference of daily motions when [the planets are moving] in the same and opposite directions. For two retrograde [planets], or for one [retrograde], divide by the sum of daily motions. //

body.text:
7.05a: labdhaṃ liptādikaṃ śodhyaṃ gate deyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
7.05b: viparyayād vakragatyor ekasmiṃs tu dhanavyayau//
body.translated_text:
The obtained result in arc-minutes etc. is to be subtracted from the past [position] and added to the future [position];
in retrograde motion, the reverse [applies]; for a single [planet], [the corrections are] additive and subtractive.

body.text:
7.06a: samāliptau bhavetāṃ tau grahau bhagaṇasaṃsthitau/
7.06b: vivaraṃ tadvad uddhṛtya dinādiphalam iṣyate//
body.translated_text:
When those two planets have equal arc-minutes in their orbital positions,
the interval is similarly extracted, and the result in days etc. is obtained.

body.text:
7.07a: kṛtvā dinakṣapāmānaṃ tathā vikṣepaliptikāH/
7.07b: natonnataṃ sādhayitvā svakāl lagnavaśāt tayoH//
body.translated_text:
Having computed the day and night durations, and likewise the latitude in arc-minutes,
having determined the north-south [positions] from their respective <s>lagna</s> (ascendant),

body.text:
7.08a: viṣuvacchāyayāmyas tadvikṣepād dvādaśoddhṛtāt/
7.08b: phalaṃ svanatanāḍīghnaṃ svadinārdhavibhājitam//
body.translated_text:
from the equinoctial shadow, the southern [correction] from their latitude divided by twelve,
the result multiplied by one's own north-south <s>nāḍīs</s> (time units), divided by one's own half-day [duration],

body.text:
7.09a: labdhaṃ prācyām ṛṇaṃ saumyād vikṣepāt paścime dhanam/
7.09b: dakṣiṇe prākkapāle svaṃ paścime tu tathā kṣamaH//
body.translated_text:
the result is subtractive in the east from a northern latitude, and additive in the west;
from a southern [latitude], it is additive in the eastern half and likewise subtractive in the western half.

body.text:
7.10a: satribhagrahajakrāntibhāgaghnāH kṣepaliptikāH/
7.10b: vikalāH svam ṛṇaṃ krāntikṣepayor bhinnatulyayoH//
body.translated_text:
The latitude in arc-minutes, multiplied by the degrees of declination produced by the planet plus three signs,
[give] arc-seconds; additive or subtractive [depending on whether] the declination and latitude are of different or same direction.

body.text:
7.11a: nakṣatragrahayogeṣu grahāstodayasādhane/
7.11b: śṛṅgonnatau tu candrasya dṛkkarmādāv idaṃ smṛtam//
body.translated_text:
In <s>nakṣatra</s>-planet conjunctions, in computing the rising and setting of planets,
and in the elevation of the crescent of the Moon, this [method] beginning with the visibility correction is prescribed.

body.text:
7.12a: tātkālikau punaH kāryau vikṣepau ca tayos tataH/
7.12b: diktulye tv antaraṃ bhede yogaH śiṣṭaṃ grahāntaram//
body.translated_text:
Then the instantaneous latitudes of those two [planets] should again be computed;
when the directions are the same, the difference [is taken]; when different, the sum; the remainder is the planetary interval.

body.text:
7.13a: kujārkijñāmarejyānāṃ triṃśadardhārdhavardhitāH/
7.13b: viṣkambhāś candrakakṣāyāṃ bhṛgoH ṣaṣṭir udāhṛtā//
body.translated_text:
For <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Arki</s> (Saturn), <s>Jña</s> (Mercury), <s>Māra</s> (unafflicted, i.e. Venus by context error — should be Moon), and <s>Ejya</s> (Jupiter), the diameters [are] thirty, increased by half and half [successively];
in the orbit of the Moon, the diameter of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) is stated as sixty.

body.text:
7.14a: tricatuH karṇayutyāptās te dvighnās trijyayā hatāH/
7.14b: sphuṭāH svakarṇās tithyāptā bhaveyur mānaliptikāH//
body.translated_text:
