Those [diameters], divided by three-fourths of the sum of the <s>karṇas</s> (hypotenuses), multiplied by two, and multiplied by the radius,
become the true [angular diameters]; divided by their own <s>karṇas</s> and by the <s>tithi</s> [factor], they become the measured arc-minutes.

body.text:
7.15a: chāyābhūmau viparyaste svacchāyāgre tu darśayet/
7.15b: grahaH svadarpaṇāntaHsthaH śaṅkvagre sampradiśyate//
body.translated_text:
On the shadow-ground, having reversed [the directions], one should mark [the planet] at the tip of its own shadow;
the planet, situated within its own mirror, is indicated at the tip of the <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon).

body.text:
7.16a: pañcahastocchritau śaṅkū yathādig bhramasaṃsthitau/
7.16b: grahāntreṇa vikṣiptāv adho hastanikhātagau//
body.translated_text:
Two <s>śaṅkus</s> (gnomons) five <s>hastas</s> (cubits) high, positioned according to direction on a turning [platform],
planted in the ground below at a depth of one <s>hasta</s>, separated by the planetary interval,

body.text:
7.17a: chāyākarṇau tato dadyāc chāyāgrāc chaṅkumūrdhagau/
7.17b: chāyākarṇāgrasaṃyoge saṃsthitasya pradarśayet//
body.translated_text:
then one should place the shadow-hypotenuses from the shadow-tips to the tops of the gnomons;
at the junction of the shadow-hypotenuse tips, one should demonstrate [the conjunction] of the [planet] situated [there].

body.text:
7.18a: svaśaṅkumūrdhagau vyomni grahau dṛktulyatām itau/
7.18b: ullekhaṃ tārakāsparśād bhede bhedaH prakīrtyate//
body.translated_text:
The two planets, [projected] at the tops of their respective gnomons in the sky, having attained visual equivalence —
contact is [declared] from the touching of stars; when separate, separation is declared.

body.text:
7.19a: yuddham aṃśuvimardākhyam aṃśuyoge parasparam/
7.19b: aṃśād ūne +apasavyākhyaṃ yuddham eko +atra ced aṇuh//
body.translated_text:
The battle called <s>aṃśu-vimarda</s> (ray-collision) [occurs] when rays mutually conjoin;
when less than [one] degree, it is called <s>apasavya</s> (left-handed) battle; if one [planet] therein is small,

body.text:
7.20a: samāgamo +aṃśād adhike bhavataś ced valānvitau/
7.20b: apasavye jito yuddhe pihito +aṇur adīptitān//
body.translated_text:
when greater than [one] degree and both are endowed with strength, it is a conjunction;
in a left-handed battle, the defeated [planet] is the small one, [rendered] without brilliance.

body.text:
7.21a: rūkṣo vivarṇo vidhvasto vijito dakṣiṇāśritaH/
7.21b: udakṣtho dīptimān sthūlo jayī yāmye +api yo balī//
body.translated_text:
The defeated one is rough, discolored, shattered, situated to the south;
the one situated to the north, brilliant, large, is the victor; also in the south, whichever is stronger [wins].

body.text:
7.22a: āsannāv apy ubhau dīptau bhavataś cet samāgamaH/
7.22b: svalpau dvāv api vidhvastau bhavetāṃ kūṭavigrahau//
body.translated_text:
If both, though near, are brilliant, it is [called] a conjunction;
if both are small and shattered, it is a <s>kūṭa-vigraha</s> (deceptive battle).

body.text:
7.23a: udakṣtho dakṣiṇastho vā bhārgavaH prāyaśo jayī/
7.23b: śaśāṅkenaivam eteṣāṃ kuryāt saṃyogasādhanam//
body.translated_text:
<s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), whether situated to the north or south, is mostly the victor;
with the Moon, one should likewise compute the conjunction of these [planets].

body.text:
7.24a: bhāvābhāvāya lokānāṃ kalpaneyaṃ pradarśitā/
7.24b: svamārgagāH prayānty ete dūram anyonyam āśritāH//
body.translated_text:
This calculation has been set forth for [predicting] the prosperity and adversity of people;
[in reality] these [planets] travel in their own paths, far away, [only appearing] close to one another.

body.text:
[nakṣatragrahayuti]
8.01a: procyante liptikā bhānāṃ svabhogo +atha daśāhataH/
8.01b: bhavanty atītadhiṣṇyānāṃ bhogaliptāyutā dhruvāH//
body.translated_text:
[Nakshatra-Planet Conjunction]
The arc-minutes of the <s>bhoga</s> (extent) of each <s>nakṣatra</s> are now stated; that [bhoga] multiplied by ten,
added to the <s>bhoga</s> arc-minutes of the passed <s>nakṣatras</s>, gives the <s>dhruvakas</s> (polar longitudes).

body.text:
8.02a: aṣṭārṇavāH śūnyakṛtāH pañcaṣaṣṭir nageṣavaH/
8.02b: aṣṭārthā abdhayo +aṣṭāgā aṅgāgā manavas tathā//

8.03a: kṛteṣavo yugarasāH śūnyavāṇā viyadrasāH/
8.03b: khavedāH sāgaranagā gajāgāH sāgarartavaH//

8.04a: manavo +atha rasā vedā vaiśvam āpyārdhabhogagam/
8.04b: āpyasyaivābhijit prānte vaiśvānte śravaṇasthitiH/
body.translated_text:
[These are the extents] of [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] up to <s>Vaiśva</s> (Uttarāṣāḍhā); <s>Āpya</s> (Pūrvāṣāḍhā) has half the extent;
<s>Abhijit</s> is at the end of <s>Āpya</s>; at the end of <s>Vaiśva</s> is the position of <s>Śravaṇa</s>.

body.text:
8.05a: tricatuH pādayoH sandhau śraviṣṭhā śravaṇasya tu/
8.05b: svabhogato viyan nāgāH ṣaṭkṛtir yamalāśvinaH//
body.translated_text:
At the junction of the third and fourth <s>pādas</s> (quarters) of <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā) [begins];
from its own extent, [the remaining extents are:] 0, 7, 6, 6, 2, 1.

body.text:
8.06a: randhrādrayaH kramād eṣāṃ vikṣepāH svād apakramāt/
8.06b: diṅmāsaviṣayāH saumye yāmye pañca diśo nava//
body.translated_text:
9, 3 — in order, these are the latitudes of these [<s>nakṣatras</s>] from their own declination;
in the northern [direction, there are] 4 with directions and 5 [others]; in the southern, 5 with directions and 9 [others].

body.text:
8.07a: saumye rasāH khaṃ yāmye +agāH saumye khārkās trayodaśa/
8.07b: dakṣiṇe rudrayamalāH saptatriṃśad athottare//
body.translated_text:
In the north: 6, 0; in the south: 8; in the north: 0, 4; thirteen;
in the south: 11, 2; thirty-seven; then in the north,

body.text:
8.08a: yāmya +adhyardhatrikakṛtā nava sārdhaśareṣavaH/
8.08b: uttarasyāṃ tathā ṣaṣṭis triṃśat ṣaṭtriṃśad eva hi//
body.translated_text:
in the south: 1.5, 3, 4; nine [and] 5.5, 7;
in the north likewise: 60, 30, 36, indeed,

body.text:
8.09a: dakṣiṇe tv ardhabhāgas tu caturviṃśatir uttare/
8.09b: bhāgāH ṣaḍviṃśatiH khaṃ ca dāsrādīnāṃ yathākramam//
body.translated_text:
in the south: half a degree; in the north: 24;
26 degrees and zero — these are [the latitudes] of [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>, in order.

body.text:
8.10a: aśītibhāgair yāmyāyām agastyo mithunāntagaH/
8.10b: viṃśe ca mithunasyāṃśe mṛgavyādho vyavasthitaH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Agastya</s> (Canopus) is situated at 80 degrees in the southern [direction], at the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini);
and <s>Mṛgavyādha</s> (Sirius) is situated at the 20th degree of <s>Mithuna</s>.

body.text:
8.11a: vikṣepo dakṣiṇe bhāgaiH khārṇavaiH svād apakramāt/
8.11b: hutabhugbrahmahṛdayau vṛṣe dvāviṃśabhāgagau//
body.translated_text:
The latitude in the southern [direction] in degrees [is] 0, 4, from its own declination;
<s>Hutabhuk</s> (Agni, i.e. the star Agni) and <s>Brahmahṛdaya</s> (Heart of Brahmā) are situated at 22 degrees in <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus),

body.text:
8.12a: aṣṭābhis triṃśatā caiva vikṣiptāv uttareṇa tau/
8.12b: golaṃ labdhvā parīkṣeta vikṣepaṃ dhruvakaṃ sphuṭam//
body.translated_text:
deflected to the north by 8 and 30 [degrees] respectively;
having obtained [their positions on] the celestial sphere, one should verify the true latitude and polar longitude.

body.text:
8.13a: vṛṣe saptadaśe bhāge yasya yāmyo +aṃśakadvayāt/
8.13b: vikṣepo +abhyadhiko bhindyād rohiṇyāH śakataṃ tu saH//
body.translated_text:
Whichever [planet] is at the 17th degree of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), having a southern latitude exceeding two degrees,
that [planet] would split the <s>śakaṭa</s> (cart, i.e. the V-shape) of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (Aldebaran).

body.text:
8.14a: grahavad dyuniśe bhānāṃ kuryād dṛkkarma pūrvavat/
8.14b: grahamelakavac cheṣaṃ grahabhuktyā dināni ca//
body.translated_text:
As for planets, one should perform the visibility correction for the day and night of the <s>nakṣatras</s> as before;
the remainder, like the planetary conjunction [method], [gives] the days by the planetary daily motion.

body.text:
8.15a: eṣyo hīne gṛhe yogo dhruvakād adhike tataH/
8.15b: viparyayād vakragate grahe jñeyaH samāgamaH//
body.translated_text:
A conjunction is to be expected when [the planet] is less than the <s>dhruvaka</s> (polar longitude) in the [zodiacal] sign; when greater, then [it is past];
for a retrograde planet, the conjunction should be understood in the reverse manner.

body.text:
8.16a: phālgunyor bhādrapadayos tathaivāṣāḍhayor dvayoH/
8.16b: viśākhāśvinisaumyānāṃ yogatārottarā smṛtā//
body.translated_text:
Of the two <s>Phālgunīs</s>, the two <s>Bhādrapadās</s>, and likewise the two <s>Āṣāḍhās</s>,
and of <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s>, the conjunction star is the northern one.

body.text:
8.17a: paścimottaratārāyā dvitīyā paścime sthitā/
8.17b: hastasya yogatārā sā śraviṣṭhāyāś ca paścimā//
body.translated_text:
The second star to the west of the northwestern star —
that is the conjunction star of <s>Hasta</s>; and [that] of <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā) is the western one.

body.text:
8.18a: jyeṣṭhāśravaṇamaitrāṇāṃ bārhaspatyasya madhyamā/
8.18b: bharaṇyāgneyapitryāṇāṃ revatyāś caiva dakṣiṇā//
body.translated_text:
Of <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s> (Maitra), and of <s>Puṣya</s> (Bārhaspatya), [it is] the middle one;
of <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s> (Āgneya), and <s>Maghā</s> (Pitrya), and of <s>Revatī</s>, [it is] the southern one.

body.text:
8.19a: rohiṇyādityamūlānāṃ prācī sārpasya caiva hi/
8.19b: yathā pratyavaśeṣāṇāṃ sthūlā syād yogatārakā//
body.translated_text:
Of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s> (Ādityā), and <s>Mūla</s>, [it is] the eastern one, and likewise of <s>Āśleṣā</s> (Sārpa);
for the remaining [<s>nakṣatras</s>], the brightest one is the conjunction star.

body.text:
8.20a: pūrvasyāṃ brahmahṛdayād aṃśakaiH pañcabhiH sthitaH/
8.20b: prajāpatir vṛṣānte +asau saumye +aṣṭatriṃśadaṃśakaiH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Prajāpati</s> is situated five degrees east of <s>Brahmahṛdaya</s>,
at the end of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), at 38 degrees to the north.

body.text:
8.21a: apāṃvatsas tu citrāyā uttare +aṃśais tu pañcabhiH/
8.21b: bṛhat kiñcid ato bhāgair āpaH ṣaḍbhis tathottare//
body.translated_text:
<s>Apāṃvatsa</s> is five degrees north of <s>Citrā</s> (Spica);
<s>Bṛhat</s> (the Great One) is slightly beyond that, six degrees further to the north.

body.text:
[udayāsta]
9.01a: athodayastamayayoH parijñānaṃ prakīrtyate/
9.01b: divākarakarākrāntamūrtinām aplatejasām//
body.translated_text:
[Heliacal Rising and Setting]
Now the understanding of [heliacal] rising and setting is declared,
of those whose forms are overwhelmed by the rays of the Sun, [rendered] of diminished brilliance.

body.text:
9.02a: sūryād abhyadhikāH paścād astaṃ jīvakujārjajāH/
9.02b: ūnāH prāgudayaṃ yānti śukrajñau vakriṇau tathā//
body.translated_text:
<s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), and <s>Arkaja</s> (Saturn), when greater [in longitude] than the Sun, set in the west;
when less, they rise in the east; <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and <s>Jña</s> (Mercury) [do so] likewise when retrograde.

body.text:
9.03a: ūnā vivasvataH prācyām astaṃ candrajñabhārgavāH/
9.03b: vrajanty abhyadhikāH pascād udayaṃ śīghrayāyinaH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Jña</s> (Mercury), and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), when less than the Sun, set in the east;
when greater, the fast-moving ones rise in the west.

body.text:
9.04a: sūryāstakālikau paścāt prācyām udayakālikau/
9.04b: divā cārkagrahau kuryād dṛkkarmātha grahasya tu//
body.translated_text:
At the time of the Sun's setting [they are visible] in the west; at the time of rising, in the east;
one should perform the visibility correction for the Sun and planet during the day; then for the planet,

body.text:
9.05a: tato lagnāntaraprāṇāḥ kālāṃśāH ṣaṣṭibhājitāH/
9.05b: pratīcyāṃ ṣaḍbhayutayos tadval lagnāntarāsavaH//
body.translated_text:
the <s>prāṇas</s> (time-units) of the interval from the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) [are computed]; the time-degrees divided by sixty,
in the west, with six [signs] added; likewise the ascensional differences of the <s>lagna</s>-interval [are found].

body.text:
9.06a: ekādaśāmarejyasya tithisaṅkhyārkajasya ca/
9.06b: astāṃśā bhūmiputrasya daśa saptādhikās tataH//
body.translated_text:
The setting degrees of <s>Māra</s> (Venus?) and <s>Ejya</s> (Jupiter) are eleven, of <s>Arkaja</s> (Saturn) the number of <s>tithis</s> (fifteen),
of <s>Bhūmiputra</s> (Mars) seventeen, and then ten more,

body.text:
9.07a: paścād astamayo +aṣṭābhir udayaH prāṅmahattayā/
9.07b: prāg astam udayaH paścād alpatvād daśabhir bhṛgoH//
body.translated_text:
setting in the west [occurs] with eight [degrees], rising in the east with greater [degrees];
rising in the east, setting in the west — <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) with ten [degrees] due to its smallness [of distance].

body.text:
9.08a: evaṃ budho dvādaśabhiś caturdaśabhir aṃśakaiH/
9.08b: vakrī śīghragatiś cārkāt karoty astmayodayau//
body.translated_text:
Likewise <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) with twelve and fourteen degrees [respectively];
a retrograde or fast-moving [planet] makes its setting and rising from the Sun [at these distances].

body.text:
9.09a: ebhyo +adhikaiH kālabhāgair dṛśyā nyūnair adarśanāH/
9.09b: bhavanti loke khacarā bhānubhāgrastamūrtayaH//
body.translated_text:
With time-degrees greater than these, [the planets] are visible; with fewer, they are invisible;
the celestial wanderers become [hidden], their forms swallowed by the rays of the Sun.

body.text:
9.10a: tatkālāṃśāntarakalā bhuktyantaravibhājitāH/
9.10b: dinādi tatphalaṃ labdhaṃ bhuktiyogena vakriṇaH//
body.translated_text:
The arc-minutes of the difference of those time-degrees, divided by the difference of [daily] motions,
give days etc. as the result; for a retrograde [planet], by the sum of the [daily] motions.

body.text:
9.11a: tallagnāsuhate bhuktī aṣṭādaśaśatoddhṛte/
9.11b: syātāṃ kālagatī tābhyāṃ dinādi gatagamyayoH//
body.translated_text:
The [daily] motions multiplied by the ascensional equivalent of that <s>lagna</s>, divided by 1800,
become the time-motions; from those two, the days etc. of the past and future [rising/setting are found].

body.text:
9.12a: svātyagastyamṛgavyādhacitrājyeṣṭhāH punarvasuH/
9.12b: abhijid brahmahṛdayaṃ trayodaśabhir aṃśakaiH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Svāti</s>, <s>Agastya</s> (Canopus), <s>Mṛgavyādha</s> (Sirius), <s>Citrā</s> (Spica), <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>,
<s>Abhijit</s>, and <s>Brahmahṛdaya</s> — [are visible] with thirteen degrees.

body.text:
9.13a: hastaśravaṇaphālgunyaH śraviṣṭā rohiṇīmaghāH/
9.13b: caturdaśāṃśakair dṛśyā viśākhāśvinidaivatam//
body.translated_text:
<s>Hasta</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, the <s>Phālgunīs</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā), <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Maghā</s> —
[are visible] with fourteen degrees; <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and [their] presiding deity [star].

body.text:
9.14a: kṛttikāmaitramūlāni sārpaṃ raudrarkṣam eva ca/
9.14b: dṛśyante pañcadaśabhir āṣāḍhād dvitayaṃ tathā//
body.translated_text: [9.14] Kṛttikā, Maitra (Anurādhā), and Mūla, as well as Sārpa (Āśleṣā) and Raudra (Ārdrā), are visible with fifteen [degrees of elongation]; likewise the two Āṣāḍhās.

body.text:
9.15a: bharaṇītiṣyasaumyāni saukṣmyāt triHsaptakāṃśakaiH/
9.15b: śeṣāṇi saptadaśabhir dṛśyādṛśyāni bhāni tu//
body.translated_text: [9.15] Bharaṇī, Tiṣya (Puṣya), and Saumya (Mṛgaśiras), on account of their faintness, [require] three-sevenths [more]; the remaining stars [require] seventeen [degrees] for their visibility and disappearance.

body.text:
9.16a: aṣṭādaśaśatābhyastā dṛśyāṃśāH svodayāsubhiH/
9.16b: vibhajya labdhāH kṣetrāṃśās tair dṛśyādṛśyatāthavā//
body.translated_text: [9.16] The visible degrees, multiplied by eighteen hundred, should be divided by one's own rising times (udayāsu); the result gives the field-degrees, by which visibility or invisibility [is determined].

body.text:
9.17a: prāg eṣām udayaH paścād asto dṛkkarma pūrvavat/
9.17b: gataiṣyadivasaprāptir bhānubhuktyā sadaiva hi//
body.translated_text: [9.17] Their rising is in the east, their setting in the west; the visibility correction is as before. The determination of elapsed and future days is always by the sun's daily motion.

body.text:
9.18a: abhijid brahmahṛdayaṃ svātīvaiṣṇavavāsavāH/
9.18b: ahirbudhnyam udakṣthatvān na lupyante +arkaraśmibhiH//
body.translated_text: [9.18] Abhijit, Brahmahṛdaya, Svātī, Vaiṣṇava (Śravaṇa), and Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), and Ahirbudhnya (Pūrvabhādrapadā) — being situated to the north, they are never obscured by the rays of the sun.

body.text:
[candraśṛṅgonna]
10.01a: udayāstavidhiH prāgvat kartavyaH śītagor api/
10.01b: bhāgair dvādaśabhiH paścād dṛśyaH prāg yāty adṛśyatām//
body.translated_text:
[Chapter on the lunar crescent]
[10.01] The procedure for rising and setting should be applied to the moon as before. She becomes visible in the west at twelve degrees [of elongation] and disappears in the east.

body.text:
10.02a: ravīndvoH ṣaḍbhayutayoH prāgval lagnāntarāsavaH/
10.02b: ekarāśau ravīndvoś ca kāryā vivaraliptikāH//
body.translated_text: [10.02] When six signs are added to the longitudes of the sun and moon, the difference in rising times is [computed] as before. When the sun and moon are in the same sign, the difference in arc-minutes should be computed.

body.text:
10.03a: tannāḍikāhate bhuktī ravīndvoH ṣaṣṭibhājite/
10.03b: tatphalānvitayor bhūyaH kartavyā vivarāsavaH//
body.translated_text: [10.03] The daily motions of the sun and moon, multiplied by those nāḍikās and divided by sixty, [give corrections]; with the results added to both, the difference in rising times should be computed again.

body.text:
10.04a: evaṃ yāvat sthirībhūtā ravīndvor antarāsavaH/
10.04b: taiH prāṇair astametīnduH śukle +arkāstamayāt param//
body.translated_text: [10.04] This [iteration continues] until the difference in rising times of the sun and moon becomes stable. By those prāṇas (time units), the moon sets after sunset in the bright fortnight.

body.text:
10.05a: bhagaṇārdhaṃ raver dattvā kāryās tadvivarāsavaH/
10.05b: taiH prāṇaiH kṛṣṇapakṣe tu śītāṃśur udayaṃ vrajet//
body.translated_text: [10.05] Adding half a revolution to the sun, one should compute the difference in rising times. By those prāṇas, in the dark fortnight, the moon rises [after the sun].

body.text:
10.06a: arkendvoH krāntiviśleṣo dikṣāmye yutir anyathā/
10.06b: tajjyendur arkād yatrāsau vijñeyā dakṣiṇottarā//
body.translated_text: [10.06] The difference of the declinations of the sun and moon [is taken] when they are on the same side; their sum when on opposite sides. The jyā (sine) of that [gives] the moon's [position relative to] the sun — it should be understood as north or south.

body.text:
10.07a: madhyāhnenduprabhākarṇasaṅguṇā yadi sottarā/
10.07b: tadārkaghnākṣajīvāyāṃ śodhyā yojyā ca dakṣiṇā//
body.translated_text: [10.07] [That result,] multiplied by the midday shadow-hypotenuse of the moon — if it is northern, it should be subtracted from, and if southern, added to, the product of the sun and the equinoctial sine (akṣajīvā).

body.text:
10.08a: śeṣaṃ lambajyayā bhaktaṃ labdho bāhuH svadiṅmukhaH/
10.08b: koṭiH śaṅkus tayor vargayuter mūlaṃ śrutir bhavet//
body.translated_text: [10.08] The remainder, divided by the cosine (lambajyā), gives the base (bāhu) in its own direction. The upright is the gnomon (śaṅku); the square root of the sum of their squares is the hypotenuse (śruti).

body.text:
10.09a: sūryonaśītagor liptāH śuklaṃ navaśatoddhṛtāH/
10.09b: candrabimbāṅgulābhyastaṃ hṛtaṃ dvādaśabhiH sphuṭam//
body.translated_text: [10.09] The arc-minutes of the moon minus the sun, in the bright fortnight, divided by nine hundred, multiplied by the moon's disc in aṅgulas and divided by twelve — [this is] the true [illuminated part].

body.text:
10.10a: dattvārkasaṃjñitaṃ binduṃ tato bāhuṃ svadiṅmukham/
10.10b: tataH paścān mukhī koṭiṃ karṇaṃ koṭyagramadhyagam//
body.translated_text: [10.10] Having placed the point designated as the sun, from there [draw] the base in its own direction, then the upright facing westward, and the hypotenuse passing through the tip of the upright.

body.text:
10.11a: koṭikarṇayutād bindor bimbaṃ tātkālikaṃ likhet/
10.11b: karṇasūtreṇa dikṣiddhiṃ prathamaṃ parikalpayet//
body.translated_text: [10.11] From the point [at the sum of] upright and hypotenuse, draw the disc at that time. With the hypotenuse-line, first determine the cardinal direction.

body.text:
10.12a: śuklaṃ karṇena tadbimbayogād antarmukhaṃ nayet/
10.12b: śuklāgrayāmyottarayor madhye matsyau prasādhayet//
body.translated_text: [10.12] The bright part, [drawn] inward from the hypotenuse to meet the disc, should be extended. Between the southern and northern tips of the bright part, construct fish-figures.

body.text: 10.13a: tanmadkhyasūtrasaṃyogād bindutrispṛg likhed dhanuH//
body.translated_text: [10.13a] From the intersection of their middle line, draw an arc touching three points of the disc.

body.text: 10.13b: prāgbimbaṃ yādṛg eva syāt tādṛk tatra dine śaśī//
body.translated_text: [10.13b] Whatever the eastern disc looks like, such is the appearance of the moon on that day.

body.text:
10.14a: koṭyā dik sādhanāt tiryakṣūtrānte śṛṅgam unnatam/
10.14b: darśayed unnatāṃ koṭiṃ kṛtvā candrasya sākṛtiH//
body.translated_text: [10.14] By establishing direction from the upright, show the elevated horn at the end of the transverse line. Having made the upright elevated, [this gives] the form of the moon.

body.text:
10.15a: kṛṣṇe ṣaḍbhayutaṃ sūryaṃ viśodhyendos tathāsitam/
10.15b: dadyād vāmaṃ bhujaṃ tatra paścimaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vidhoH//
body.translated_text: [10.15] In the dark fortnight, add six signs to the sun and subtract from the moon; thus [one obtains] the dark [portion]. One should give the base to the left — there [one draws] the western disc of the moon.

body.text:
[pāta]
11.01a: ekāyanagatau syātāṃ sūryacandramasau yadā/
11.01b: tadyutau maṇḍale krāntyos tulyatve vaidhṛtābhidhaH//
body.translated_text:
[Chapter on Vyatīpāta (malefic conjunction)]
[11.01] When the sun and moon move in the same ayana (solstitial half), at the time when their declinations on the ecliptic become equal, [the conjunction] is called Vaidhṛta.

body.text:
11.02a: viparītāyanagatau candrārkau krāntiliptikā/
11.02b: samās tadā vyatīpāto bhagaṇārdhe tayor yutau//
body.translated_text: [11.02] When the moon and sun move in opposite ayanas, and their declination arc-minutes are equal, then it is Vyatīpāta; [this occurs] when their combined [longitudes equal] half a revolution.

body.text:
11.03a: tulyāṃśujālasamparkāt tayos tu pravahāhataH/
11.03b: taddṛkkrodhabhavo vahnir lokābhāvāya jāyate//
body.translated_text: [11.03] From the contact of their equal rays, struck by the Pravaha wind, a fire born of their wrathful gaze arises for the destruction of the worlds.

body.text:
11.04a: vināśayati pāto +asmin lokānām asakṛd yataH/
11.04b: vyatīpātaH prasiddho +ayaṃ sañjñābhedena vaidhṛtaH//
body.translated_text: [11.04] Since this pāta (conjunction) repeatedly destroys the worlds, this Vyatīpāta is well known — [also called] Vaidhṛta by a different name.

body.text:
11.05a: sa kṛṣṇo dāruṇavapur lohitākṣo mahodaraH/
11.05b: sarvāniṣṭakaro raudro bhūyo bhūyaH prajāyate//
body.translated_text: [11.05] He is dark, of terrible form, red-eyed, great-bellied, causing all misfortune, fierce — and he is born again and again.

body.text:
11.06a: bhāskarendvor bhacakrāntaś cakrārdhāvadhisaṃsthayoH/
11.06b: dṛktulyasādhitāṃśādiyuktayoH svāv apakramau//
body.translated_text: [11.06] The declinations of the sun and moon, within the zodiac up to the limit of half a revolution, should be corrected with degrees etc. established by observation.

body.text:
11.07a: athaujapadagasyendoH krāntir vikṣepasaṃskṛtā/
11.07b: yadi syād adhikā bhānoH krānteH pāto gatas tadā//
body.translated_text: [11.07] Then, if the declination of the moon in an odd quadrant, corrected by the latitude (vikṣepa), is greater than the sun's declination, the pāta has passed.

body.text:
11.08a: ūnā cet syāt tadā bhāvī vāmaṃ yugmapadasya ca/
11.08b: padānyatvaṃ vidhoH krāntivikṣepāc ced viśudhyati//
body.translated_text: [11.08] If it is less, then [the pāta] is yet to come. For an even quadrant, [the rule is] reversed. If the quadrant-nature of the moon is rectified from the declination and latitude —

body.text:
11.09a: krāntyor jye trijyayābhyaste parakrāntijyayoddhṛte/
11.09b: taccāpāntaram ardhaṃ vā yojyaṃ bhāvini śītagau//
body.translated_text: [11.09] The sines of both declinations, multiplied by the radius and divided by the sine of maximum declination — [the difference of] their arcs, or half [of it], should be applied to the moon when [the pāta] is future,

body.text:
11.10a: śodhyaṃ candrād gate pāte tatsūryagatitāḍitam/
11.10b: candrabhuktyā hṛtaṃ bhānau liptādi śaśivat phalam//
body.translated_text: [11.10] and subtracted from the moon when [the pāta] has passed. That [result], multiplied by the sun's daily motion and divided by the moon's daily motion, gives the correction in arc-minutes for the sun; likewise for the moon.

body.text:
11.11a: tadvacchaśāṅkapātasya phalaṃ deyaṃ viparyayāt/
11.11b: karmaitad asakṛt tāvad yāvad krāntī same tayoH//
body.translated_text: [11.11] Similarly, the correction for the moon's node should be applied in the reverse manner. This procedure [should be repeated] as many times as needed until the two declinations become equal.

body.text:
11.12a: krāntyoH samatve pāto +atha prakṣiptāṃśonite vidhau/
11.12b: hīne +ardharātrikād yāto bhāvī tātkālike +adhike//
body.translated_text: [11.12] When the declinations are equal, the pāta [occurs]. When the corrected degrees are applied to the moon — if less than [the longitude at] midnight, [the pāta] has passed; if more at that moment, it is yet to come.

body.text:
11.13a: sthirīkṛtārdharātrendvor dvayor vivaraliptikāH/
11.13b: ṣaṣṭighnyaś candrabhuktyāptāH pātakālasya nāḍikāH//
body.translated_text: [11.13] The difference in arc-minutes between the stabilized midnight moon and the other, multiplied by sixty and divided by the moon's daily motion, gives the nāḍikās of the pāta time.

body.text:
11.14a: ravīndumānayogārdhaṃ ṣaṣṭyā saṅguṇya bhājayet/
11.14b: tayor bhuktyantareṇāptaṃ sthityardhaṃ nāḍikādi tat//
body.translated_text: [11.14] Half the sum of the diameters of the sun and moon, multiplied by sixty, should be divided by the difference of their daily motions; the result is the half-duration in nāḍikās etc.

body.text:
11.15a: pātakālaH sphuṭo madhyaH so +api sthityardhavarjitaH/
11.15b: tasya sambhavakālaH syāt tat saṃyukto +antyasāṃjñitaH//
body.translated_text: [11.15] The true mid-point is the pāta time. That minus the half-duration gives the beginning time; that plus [the half-duration] gives [the time] called the end.

body.text:
11.16a: ādyantakālayor madhyaH kālo jñeyo +atidāruṇaH/
11.16b: prajvalaj jvalanākāraH sarvakarmasu garhitaH//
body.translated_text: [11.16] The middle time between the beginning and end should be known as extremely dangerous — blazing like fire, condemned in all rites.

body.text:
11.17a: ekāyanagataṃ yāvad arkendvor maṇḍalāntaram/
11.17b: sambhavas tāvad evāsya sarvakarmavināśakṛt//
body.translated_text: [11.17] As long as the interval between the sun's and moon's ecliptic [longitudes] is within the same ayana [and within half a revolution], the occurrence of this [pāta], which destroys all rites, is possible.

body.text:
11.18a: snānadānajapaśrāddhavratahomādikarmabhiH/
11.18b: prāpyata sumahacchreyas tatkālajñānatas tathā//
body.translated_text: [11.18] By acts of bathing, charity, recitation, śrāddha (ancestral rites), vows, fire-offerings, and other rituals, great merit is obtained through knowledge of that time.

body.text:
11.19a: ravīndvos tulyatā krāntyor viṣuvatsannidhau yadā/
11.19b: dvir bhaved dhi tadā pātaH syād abhāvo viparyayāt//
body.translated_text: [11.19] When the equality of the declinations of the sun and moon occurs near the equinox, the pāta occurs twice; in the reverse [situation], there is no occurrence.

body.text:
11.20a: śasāṅkārkayuter liptā bhabhogena vibhājitāH/
11.20b: labdhaṃ saptadaśānto +anyo vyatīpātas tṛtīyakaH//
body.translated_text: [11.20] The arc-minutes of the sum of the moon and sun, divided by the daily motion of the asterism (bhabhoga), give another result — up to the seventeenth [yoga] is the third vyatīpāta.

body.text:
11.21a: sārpendrapauṣṇyadhiṣṇyānām antyāH pādā bhasandhayaH/
11.21b: tadagrabheṣv ādyapādo gaṇḍāntaṃ nāma kīrtyate//
body.translated_text: [11.21] The last quarters of Sārpa (Āśleṣā), Aindra (Jyeṣṭhā), and Pauṣṇya (Revatī) asterisms are the junctions of the signs. The first quarter of [the asterisms] following those is called gaṇḍānta (knot-end).

body.text:
11.22a: vyatīpātatrayaṃ ghoraṃ gaṇḍāntatritayaṃ tathā/
11.22b: etad bhasandhitritayaṃ sarvakarmasu varjayet//
body.translated_text: [11.22] The three vyatīpātas are terrible, and likewise the three gaṇḍāntas. These three sign-junctions should be avoided in all rites.

body.text:
11.23a: ity etat paramaṃ puṇyaṃ jyotiṣāṃ caritaṃ hitam/
11.23b: rhasyaṃ mahad ākhyātaṃ kim anyacchrotum icchasi//
body.translated_text: [11.23] Thus has been declared this supremely meritorious, beneficial account of the luminaries — a great secret. What else do you wish to hear?

body.text:
[bhūgola]
12.01a: athārkāṃśasamudbhūtaṃ praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliH/
12.01b: bhaktyā paramayābhyarcya papracchedaṃ mayāsuraH//
body.translated_text:
[Chapter on the Earth-globe]
[12.01] Then, prostrating himself before the [deity] born from a portion of the sun, with joined palms and supreme devotion, Maya the Asura asked this:

body.text:
12.02a: bhagavan kimpramāṇā bhūH kim ākārā kim āśrayā/
12.02b: kiṃvibhāgā kathaṃ cātra saptapātālabhūmayaH//
body.translated_text: [12.02] 'O Blessed One, what is the measure of the earth? What is its shape? What is its support? What are its divisions? And how are the seven underworlds and surface-lands [arranged] upon it?'

body.text:
12.03a: ahorātravyavasthāṃ ca vidadhāti kathaṃ raviH/
12.03b: kathaṃ paryeti vasudhāṃ bhuvanāni vibhāvayan//
body.translated_text: [12.03] 'And how does the sun establish the cycle of day and night? How does it traverse the earth, illuminating the worlds?'

body.text:
12.04a: devāsurāṇām anyonyam ahorātraṃ viparyayāt/
12.04b: kim atha tat kathaṃ vā syād bhānor bhagaṇapūraṇāt//
body.translated_text: [12.04] 'Day and night for the Devas and Asuras are mutually reversed — how is that, and how does it come about from the sun's completion of a revolution?'

body.text:
12.05a: pitryaṃ māsena bhavati nāḍīṣaṣṭyā tu mānuṣam/
12.05b: tad eva kila sarvatra na bhavet kena hetunā//
body.translated_text: [12.05] 'A month [of ours] constitutes a day for the Pitṛs (ancestors), and sixty nāḍikās a human [day]. If that is indeed the same everywhere, why is it not [so]? For what reason?'

body.text:
12.06a: dinābdamāsahorāṇām adhipā na samāH kutaH/
12.06b: kathaṃ paryeti bhagaṇaH sagraho +ayaṃ kim āśrayaH//
body.translated_text: [12.06] 'Why are the lords of the day, year, month, and hour not the same? How does this revolution of the planets proceed, and on what does it rest?'

body.text:
12.07a: bhūmer uparyuparyūrdhvāH kim utsedhāH kim antarāH/
12.07b: graharkṣakakṣāH kiṃmātrāH sthitāH kena krameṇa tāH//
body.translated_text: [12.07] 'Above the earth, one above another — what are the heights? What are the intervals? What are the measures of the orbits of planets and stars? And in what order are they situated?'

body.text:
12.08a: grīṣme tīvrakaro bhānur na hemante tathāvidhaH/
12.08b: kiyatī tatkaraprāptir mānāni kati kiṃ ca taiH//
body.translated_text: [12.08] 'In summer, the sun's rays are fierce, but not so in winter — what is the extent of the reach of its rays? How many are the measures, and what [is accomplished] by them?'

body.text:
12.09a: evaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chindhi bhagavan bhūtabhāvana/
12.09b: anyo na tvām ṛte chettā vidyate sarvadarśivān//
body.translated_text: [12.09] 'Thus resolve my doubt, O Blessed One, creator of beings. There is no other resolver besides you, who sees all.'

body.text:
12.10a: iti bhaktyoditaṃ śrutvā mayoktaṃ vākyam asya hi/
12.10b: rahasyaṃ param adhyāyaṃ tataH prāha punaH sa tam//
body.translated_text: [12.10] Having heard this speech uttered with devotion by Maya, he (the solar deity) then spoke again to him the supreme secret chapter.

body.text:
12.11a: śṛṇuṣvaikamanā bhūtvā guhyam adhyātma saṃjñitam/
12.11b: pravakṣyāmy atibhaktānāṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate mama//
body.translated_text:
Having become single-minded, listen to this secret known as <s>adhyātma</s> (the supreme self);
I shall declare it — nothing is to be withheld from those of supreme devotion.

body.text:
12.12a: vāsudevaH paraṃ brahma tanmūrtiH puruṣaH paraH/
12.12b: avyakto nirguṇaH śāntaH pañcaviṃśāt paro +avyayaH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; His form is the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person),
unmanifest, without qualities, tranquil, beyond the twenty-fifth [principle], imperishable.

body.text:
12.13a: prakṛtyantargato devo bahir antaś ca sarvagaH/
12.13b: saṅkarṣaṇo +apaH sṛṣṭvādau tāsu vīryam avāsṛjat//
body.translated_text:
The God who dwells within <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), all-pervading both within and without —
as <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, He first created the waters and deposited His potency in them.

body.text:
12.14a: tadaṇḍam abhavad dhaimaṃ sarvatra tamasāvṛtam/
12.14b: tatrāniruddhaH prathamaṃ vyaktībhūtaH sanātanaH//
body.translated_text:
From that arose a golden egg, enveloped everywhere by darkness;
therein <s>Aniruddha</s>, the eternal one, first became manifest.

body.text:
12.15a: hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān eṣa chandasi paṭhyate/
12.15b: ādityo hy ādibhūtatvāt prasūtyā sūrya ucyate//
body.translated_text:
This glorious one is celebrated in the <s>Vedas</s> as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the golden embryo);
He is called <s>Āditya</s> because He is the primordial being, and <s>Sūrya</s> because of [His] emanation.

body.text:
12.16a: paraṃ jyotis tamaH pāre sūryo +ayaṃ saviteti ca/
12.16b: paryeti bhuvanān eṣa bhāvayan bhūtabhāvanaH//
body.translated_text:
The supreme light beyond darkness — this <s>Sūrya</s> is also called <s>Savitṛ</s> (the impeller);
He traverses the worlds, vivifying [them], the creator of beings.

body.text:
12.17a: prakāśātmā tamohantā mahān ity eṣa viśrutaH/
12.17b: ṛco +asya maṇḍalaṃ sāmānyustrāmūrtir yajūṃṣi ca//
body.translated_text:
Being of the nature of light, the destroyer of darkness, He is renowned as <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One);
the <s>Ṛc</s> verses are His disc, the <s>Sāman</s> chants [His other form], and the <s>Yajus</s> formulae are His embodiment.

body.text:
12.18a: trayīmaho +ayaṃ bhagavāṇ kālātmā kālakṛd vibhuH/
12.18b: sarvātmā sarvagaH sūkṣmaH sarvam asmin pratiṣṭhitam//
body.translated_text:
This glorious Lord, whose greatness is the threefold <s>Veda</s>, is the soul of time, the maker of time, all-pervading;
He is the soul of all, omnipresent, subtle — everything is established in Him.

body.text:
12.19a: rathe viśvamaye cakraṃ kṛtvā saṃvatsarātmakam/
12.19b: chandāṃsy aśvāH sapta yuktāH paryaṭaty eṣa sarvadā//
body.translated_text:
Having made a wheel of the nature of the year upon His chariot that is the entire universe,
with the <s>chandas</s> (Vedic meters) as seven yoked horses, He always travels about.

body.text:
12.20a: tripādam amṛtaṃ guhyaṃ pādo +ayaṃ prakaṭo +abhavat/
12.20b: so +ahaṅkāraṃ jagatsṛṣṭyai brahmāṇam asṛjat prabhuH//
body.translated_text:
Three-quarters [of Him] is immortal and hidden; this one quarter became manifest;
He, the Lord, created <s>Brahmā</s> along with <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) for the purpose of creating the world.

body.text:
12.21a: tasmai vedān varān dattvā sarvalokapitāmaham/
12.21b: pratiṣṭhāpyāṇḍamadhye +atha svayaṃ paryeti bhāvayan//
body.translated_text:
Having given him the <s>Vedas</s> as boons and established him as the grandfather of all worlds
in the midst of the [cosmic] egg, He himself revolves about, vivifying [all].

body.text:
12.22a: atha sṛṣṭyāṃ manaś cakre brahmāhaṅkāramūrtibhṛt/
12.22b: manasaś candramā jajñe sūryo +akṣṇos tejasāṃ nidhiH//
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, bearing the form of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), directed his mind toward creation;
from the mind was born the Moon, and from the eyes the Sun, the treasury of radiance.

body.text:
12.23a: manasaH khaṃ tato vāyur agnir āpo dharā kramāt/
12.23b: guṇaikavṛddhyā pañcaiva mahābhūtāni jajñire//
body.translated_text:
From the mind [arose] space, then wind, fire, water, and earth in succession;
with a progressive increase of one quality [each], the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) were born.

body.text:
12.24a: agnīṣomau bhānucandrau tatas tv aṅgārakādayaH/
12.24b: tejobhūkhāmbuvātebhyaH kramaśaH pañca jajñire//
body.translated_text:
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) and <s>Soma</s> (Moon), the Sun and Moon [were first]; then <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars) and the others —
from fire, earth, space, water, and wind respectively, the five [planets] were born in order.

body.text:
12.25a: punar dvādaśadhātmānaṃ vyabhajad rāśisañjñakam/
12.25b: nakṣatrarūpiṇaṃ bhūyaH saptaviṃśātmakaṃ vaśī//
body.translated_text:
He then divided himself twelvefold, designated as the <s>rāśis</s> (zodiacal signs),
and again into the form of twenty-seven <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), the self-controlled one.

body.text:
12.26a: tataś carācaraṃ viśvaṃ nirmame devapūrvakam/
12.26b: ūrdhvamadhyādharebhyo +atha srotobhyaH prakṛtīH sṛjan//
body.translated_text:
Then He fashioned the entire universe of moving and unmoving beings, beginning with the gods,
creating the elements from the upper, middle, and lower channels.

body.text:
12.27a: guṇakarmavibhāgena sṛṣṭvā prāgvad anukramāt/
12.27b: vibhāgaṃ kalpayāmāsa yathāsvaṃ vedadarśanāt//
body.translated_text:
Having created [beings] by the division of qualities and actions as before, in due order,
He assigned the divisions to each according to the vision of the <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text:
12.28a: grahanakṣatratārānāṃ bhūmer viśvasya vā vibhuH/
12.28b: devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ siddhānāṃ ca yathākramam//
body.translated_text:
The all-pervading Lord [assigned divisions] to planets, <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), and stars, to the earth and the universe,
to gods, <s>asuras</s> (demons), humans, and <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), each in proper order.

body.text:
12.29a: brahmāṇḍam etat suṣiraṃ tatredaṃ bhūrbhuvādikam/
12.29b: kaṭāhadvitayasyeva sampuṭaṃ golakākṛti//
body.translated_text:
This <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) is hollow; within it is this [realm] of <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvar</s>, and so forth,
like the seal-joint of two half-shells, spherical in shape.

body.text:
12.30a: brahmāṇḍamadhye paridhir vyomakakṣābhidhīyate/
12.30b: tanmadhye bhramaṇaṃ bhānām adho +adhaH kramaśas tathā//
body.translated_text:
In the middle of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>, the circumference is called the <s>vyomakakṣā</s> (orbit of space);
within that, the revolution of the luminaries [proceeds] progressively lower and lower.

body.text:
12.31a: mandāmarejyabhūputrasūryaśukrendujendavaH/
12.31b: paribhramanty adho+adhaHsthāH siddhhavidyādharā ghanāH//
body.translated_text:
<s>Manda</s> (Saturn), <s>Amara-ijya</s> (Jupiter), <s>Bhūputra</s> (Mars), <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Indu-ja</s> (Mercury), and <s>Indu</s> (the Moon) —
they revolve positioned progressively lower; [below them are] the <s>siddhas</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, and clouds.

body.text:
12.32a: madhye samantād aṇḍasya bhūgolo vyomni tiṣṭhati/
12.32b: bibhrānaH paramāṃ śaktiṃ brahmaṇo dhāraṇātmakām//
body.translated_text:
In the middle of the [cosmic] egg on all sides, the terrestrial globe stands in space,
supported by the supreme power of <s>Brahmā</s>, which is of the nature of sustaining.

body.text:
12.33a: tadantarapuṭāH sapta nāgāsurasamāśrayāH/
12.33b: divyauṣadhirasopetā ramyāH pātālabhūmayaH//
body.translated_text:
Within it are seven interior shells, the abode of <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) and <s>Asuras</s> (demons),
endowed with the essences of divine herbs — the delightful <s>Pātāla</s> (netherworld) regions.

body.text:
12.34a: anekaratnanicayo jāmbūnadamayo giriH/
12.34b: bhūgolamadhyago merur ubhayatra vinirgataH//
body.translated_text:
A mountain of numerous gems, made of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> (gold) —
<s>Meru</s>, situated at the center of the terrestrial globe, projects on both sides.

body.text:
12.35a: upariṣṭāt sthitās tasya sendrā devā maharṣayaH/
12.35b: adhastād asurās tadvad dviṣanto +anyonyam āśritāH//
body.translated_text:
Above it dwell the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, and the great sages;
below it likewise dwell the <s>asuras</s>, mutually hostile, dependent on one another.

body.text:
12.36a: tataH samantāt paridhiH krameṇāyaṃ mahārṇavaH/
12.36b: mekhaleva sthito dhātryā devāsuravibhāgakṛt//
body.translated_text:
Then all around, this great ocean [forms] a circumference in succession,
situated like a girdle of the earth, creating the division between gods and <s>asuras</s>.

body.text:
12.37a: samantān merumadhyāt tu tulyabhāgeṣu toyadheH/
12.37b: dvīpiṣu dikṣu pūrvādinagaryo devanirmitāH//
body.translated_text:
At equal distances from the center of <s>Meru</s> on all sides, upon the ocean,
on the <s>dvīpas</s> (continents) in the cardinal directions beginning with the east, are cities built by the gods.

body.text:
12.38a: bhūvṛttapāde pūrvasyāṃ yamakoṭīti viśrutā/
12.38b: bhadrāśvavarṣe nagarī svarṇaprākāratoraṇā//
body.translated_text:
At one-quarter of the earth's circumference, in the east, is the renowned [city] called <s>Yamakoṭī</s>,
a city in <s>Bhadrāśva-varṣa</s>, with ramparts and gateways of gold.

body.text:
12.39a: yāmyāyāṃ bhārate varṣe laṅkā tadvan mahāpurī/
12.39b: paścime ketumālākhye romakākhyā prakīrtitā//
body.translated_text:
In the south, in <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s>, is <s>Laṅkā</s>, a similarly great city;
in the west, in the land called <s>Ketumāla</s>, [the city] known as <s>Romaka</s> is celebrated.

body.text:
12.40a: udak siddhapurī nāma kuruvarṣe prakīrtitā/
12.40b: tasyāṃ siddhā mahātmāno nivasanti gatavyathāH//
body.translated_text:
In the north, the city called <s>Siddhapurī</s> is celebrated in <s>Kuru-varṣa</s>;
in it dwell the great-souled <s>Siddhas</s>, free from affliction.

body.text:
12.41a: bhūvṛttapādavivarās tāś cānyonyaṃ pratiṣṭhitāH/
12.41b: tābhyaś cottarago merus tāvān eva surāśrayaH//
body.translated_text:
These [cities] are separated from one another by one-quarter of the earth's circumference;
<s>Meru</s> is equally [one-quarter] north of them, the abode of the gods.

body.text:
12.42a: tāsām uparigo yāti viṣuvastho divākaraH/
12.42b: na tāsu viṣuvacchāyā nākṣasyonnatir iṣyate//
body.translated_text:
The Sun, when at the equinox, passes over those [cities];
at those [cities] there is no equinoctial shadow, and no elevation of the [celestial] pole is admitted.

body.text:
12.43a: meror ubhayato madhye dhruvatāre nabhaH sthite/
12.43b: nirakṣadeśasaṃsthānām ubhaye kṣitijāśraye//
body.translated_text:
On both sides of <s>Meru</s>, at the midpoint, the two pole stars are situated in the sky;
for those dwelling at the equator, both [poles] rest on the horizon.

body.text:
12.44a: ato nākṣatrocchrayas tāsu dhruvayoH kṣitijasthayoH/
12.44b: navatir lambakāṃśās tu merāvakṣāṃśakās tathā/
body.translated_text:
Therefore at those [equatorial cities] there is no elevation of the pole [above the horizon], as both poles rest on the horizon;
but at <s>Meru</s>, ninety degrees is the <s>lambaka</s> (co-latitude), and likewise the <s>akṣa</s> (latitude) degrees.

body.text:
12.45a: meṣādau devabhāgasthe devānāṃ yāti darśanam/
12.45b: asurāṇāṃ tulādau tu sūryas tadbhāgasañcaraH//
body.translated_text:
When the Sun is situated in the gods' portion [of the sky] beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), it comes into view of the gods;
when [it is] at the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), the Sun traverses the <s>asuras</s>' portion.

body.text:
12.46a: atyāsannatayā tena grīṣme tīvrakarā raveH/
12.46b: devabhāge surāṇāṃ tu hemante mandatānyathā//
body.translated_text:
Due to its great proximity, the Sun's rays are intense in summer
in the gods' portion for the gods; in winter [they are] mild, and the reverse in the <s>asuras</s>' portion.

body.text:
12.47a: devāsurā viṣuvati kṣitijasthaṃ divākaram/
12.47b: paśyanty anyonyam eteṣāṃ vāmasavye dinakṣape//
body.translated_text:
At the equinoxes, gods and <s>asuras</s> see the Sun situated on the horizon;
for these [two groups], day and night are reversed, [proceeding] leftward and rightward.

body.text:
12.48a: meṣādāv uditaH sūryas trīn rāśīn udaguttaram/
12.48b: sañcaran prāgaharmadhyaṃ pūrayen meruvāsinām//
body.translated_text:
The Sun, having risen at the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), traversing three signs northward,
fills the forenoon for the inhabitants of <s>Meru</s>.

body.text:
12.49a: *karkyādīn sañcaraṃś tadvad ahnaH paścārdham eva saH/(C karkādīn)
12.49b: tulādīṃs trīn mṛgādīṃś ca tadvad eva suradviṣām//
body.translated_text:
Traversing [the signs] beginning with <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) similarly, it [fills] the latter half of the day;
[the signs] beginning with <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) — three — and beginning with <s>Mṛga</s> (Capricorn) — likewise for the enemies of the gods.

body.text:
12.50a: ato dinakṣape teṣām anyonyaṃ hi viparyayāt/
12.50b: ahorātrapramāṇaṃ ca bhānor bhagaṇapūraṇāt//
body.translated_text:
Therefore the day and night of these [gods and <s>asuras</s>] are mutually reversed;
the measure of day and night [for them] equals one full revolution of the Sun.

body.text:
12.51a: dinakṣapārdham eteṣām ayanānte viparyayāt/
12.51b: uparyātmānam anyonyaṃ kalpayanti surāsurāH//
body.translated_text:
Half of the day and night of these [beings is determined] at the solstice by reversal;
the gods and <s>asuras</s> consider themselves to be above one another.

body.text:
12.52a: anye +api samasūtrasthā manyante +adhaH parasparam/
12.52b: bhadrāśvaketumālasthā laṅkāsiddhapurāśritāH//
body.translated_text:
Others too, situated on the same diameter, consider each other to be below —
those dwelling in <s>Bhadrāśva</s> and <s>Ketumāla</s>, and those in <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Siddhapurī</s>.

body.text:
12.53a: sarvatraiva mahīgole svasthānam upari sthitam/
12.53b: manyante khe yato golas tasya kvordhavaṃ kva vādhaH//
body.translated_text:
Everywhere on the terrestrial globe, [beings] consider their own place to be on top;
since the globe is in space, where indeed is its top and where its bottom?

body.text:
12.54a: alpakāyatayā lokāH svasthānāt sarvato mukham/
12.54b: paśyanti vṛttām apy etāṃ cakrākārāṃ vasundharām//
body.translated_text:
Due to the smallness of their own size, people from their own place see [the earth as flat] in all directions,
perceiving this [earth], though round, as being circular [i.e., flat] like a disc.

body.text:
12.55a: savyaṃ bhramati devānām apasavyaṃ suradviṣām/
12.55b: upariṣṭād bhagolo +ayaṃ vyakṣe paścān mukhaH sadā//
body.translated_text:
The celestial sphere revolves leftward for the gods, rightward for the enemies of the gods;
for those at the equator, this stellar sphere always faces westward from above.

body.text:
12.56a: atas tatra dinaṃ triṃśannāḍikaṃ śarvadī tathā/
12.56b: hānivṛddhī sadā vāmaṃ surāsuravibhāgayoH//
body.translated_text:
Therefore, there the day is of thirty <s>nāḍikās</s> (half-watches), and the night likewise;
increase and decrease [of day and night] always [proceed] leftward in the divisions of gods and <s>asuras</s>.

body.text:
12.57a: meṣādau tu sadā vṛddhir udaguttarato +adhikā/
12.57b: devāṃśe ca kṣapāhānir viparītaṃ tathāsure//
body.translated_text:
Beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), there is always increase, greater toward the north,
in the gods' portion; and decrease of night — the reverse in the <s>asuras</s>' portion.

body.text:
12.58a: tulādau dyuniśor vāmaṃ kṣayavṛddhī tayor ubhe/
12.58b: deśakrāntivaśān nityaṃ tadvijñānaṃ puroditam//
body.translated_text:
At the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), the decrease and increase of day and night for those two [groups] are both leftward;
this knowledge [of variation] is always dependent on the local latitude and declination, as stated earlier.

body.text:
12.59a: bhūvṛttaṃ krāntibhāgaghnaṃ bhagaṇāṃśavibhājitam/
12.59b: avāptayojanair arko vyakṣād yāty uparisthitaH//
body.translated_text:
The earth's circumference multiplied by the degrees of declination, divided by the degrees in a full revolution,
gives <s>yojanas</s>; by that [amount] the Sun travels above from the equator.

body.text:
12.60a: paramāpakramād evaṃ yojanāni viśodhayet/
12.60b: bhūvṛttapādāc cheṣāṇi yāni syur yojanāni taiH//
body.translated_text:
From the maximum declination one should thus subtract [those] <s>yojanas</s>;
the <s>yojanas</s> remaining from one-quarter of the earth's circumference — by those,

body.text:
12.61a: ayanānte vilomena devāsuravibhāgayoH/
12.61b: nāḍīṣaṣṭyā sakṛd aharniśāpy asmin sakṛt tathā//
body.translated_text:
at the solstice, in reverse order for the divisions of gods and <s>asuras</s>,
sixty <s>nāḍikās</s> constitute one day, and likewise one night, once [each].

body.text:
12.62a: tadantare +api ṣaṣṭyante kṣayavṛddhī aharniśoH/
12.62b: parato viparīto +ayaṃ bhagolaH parivartate//
body.translated_text:
In the interval between those [solstices] also, at the end of sixty [<s>nāḍikās</s>], there is decrease and increase of day and night;
beyond that, the stellar sphere revolves in the opposite direction.

body.text:
12.63a: ūne bhūvṛttapāde tu dvijyāpakramayojanaiH/
12.63b: dhanur mṛgasthaH savitā devabhāge na dṛśyate//
body.translated_text:
When less than one-quarter of the earth's circumference by the <s>yojanas</s> of the double-sine of declination,
the Sun situated in <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius) and <s>Mṛga</s> (Capricorn) is not visible in the gods' portion.

body.text:
12.64a: tathā cāsurabhāge tu mithune karkaṭe sthitaH/
12.64b: naṣṭacchāyā mahīvṛttapāde darśanam ādiśet//
body.translated_text:
Likewise in the <s>asuras</s>' portion, [the Sun] situated in <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) and <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer)
[produces] no shadow; [for those] at one-quarter of the earth's circumference, it indicates [the limit of] visibility.

body.text:
12.65a: ekajyāpakramānītair yojanaiH parivarjite/
12.65b: bhūmikakṣācaturthāṃśe vyakṣāc cheṣais tu yojanaiH//
body.translated_text: In the quarter of the earth's orbit diminished by the <s>yojanas</s> derived from the sine of the declination, with the remaining <s>yojanas</s> without latitude — //

body.text:
12.66a: dhanur mṛgālikumbheṣu saṃsthito +arko na dṛśyate/
12.66b: devabhāge +asurāṇāṃ tu vṛṣādye bhacatuṣṭaye//
body.translated_text: The Sun, stationed in [the signs] Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces, is not seen in the realm of the gods; [it is not seen] by the <s>asuras</s> in the four signs beginning with Taurus. //

body.text:
12.67a: merau *meṣādicakrārdhe devāH paśyanti bhāskaram/(ḍ -cakārdhe)
12.67b: sakṛd evoditaṃ tadvad asurāś ca tulādigam//
body.translated_text: At <s>Meru</s>, the gods see the Sun once risen in the half-circle beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries); likewise the <s>asuras</s> [see it once risen] in [the half beginning with] <s>Tulā</s> (Libra). //

body.text:
12.68a: bhūmaṇḍalāt pañcadaśe bhāge deve +atha vāsure/
12.68b: upariṣṭād vrajaty arkaH saumyayāmyāyanāntagaH//
body.translated_text: At a fifteenth part [of the circumference] from the earth's equator, in the realm of the gods or the <s>asuras</s>, the Sun moves overhead, moving between the solstices. //

body.text:
12.69a: tadantarālayoś cchāyā yāmyodak sambhavaty api/
12.69b: meror abhimukhaṃ yāti parataH svavibhāgayoH//
body.translated_text: In the regions between those two, the shadow falls south and north; facing <s>Meru</s>, it moves; beyond, in their own divisions. //

body.text:
12.70a: bhadrāśvoparigaH kuryād bhārate tūdayaṃ raviH/
12.70b: rātryardhaṃ ketumāle tu kurāv astamayaṃ tadā//
body.translated_text: When the Sun rises over <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, it causes sunrise in <s>Bhārata</s>; it is midnight in <s>Ketumāla</s>; and it sets in <s>Kuru</s> at that time. //

body.text:
12.71a: bhāratādiṣu varṣeṣu tadvad eva paribhraman/
12.71b: madhyodayārdharātryastakālān kuryāt pradakṣiṇam//
body.translated_text: Revolving likewise over the continents beginning with <s>Bhārata</s>, it creates midday, sunrise, midnight, and sunset times in a clockwise [circuit]. //

body.text:
12.72a: dhruvonnatir bhacakrasya natir meruṃ prayāsyataH/
12.72b: nirakṣābhimukhaṃ yātur viparīte natonnate//
body.translated_text: The elevation of the pole star is the altitude [of the pole]; the depression of the zodiac [is] toward <s>Meru</s> for one going [northward]. For one going toward the equator, the altitude and depression are reversed. //

body.text:
12.73a: bhacakraṃ dhruvayor baddham ākṣiptaṃ pravahānilaiH/
12.73b: paryety ajasraṃ tannaddhā grahakakṣā yathākramam//
body.translated_text: The zodiacal circle, fastened at the two poles, driven by the <s>Pravaha</s> winds, revolves constantly; bound to it, the orbits of the planets [revolve] in succession. //

body.text:
12.74a: sakṛd udgatam abdārdhaṃ paśyanty arkaṃ surāsurāH/
12.74b: pitaraH śaśigāH pakṣaṃ svadinaṃ ca narā bhuvi//
body.translated_text: The gods and <s>asuras</s> see the Sun, once risen, for half a year. The <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), [dwelling] at the Moon['s path], [see it for] a fortnight; and humans on earth [see it for] their own day. //

body.text:
12.75a: *upariṣṭasya mahatī kakṣālpādhaHsthitasya ca/(C upariṣṭhasya)
12.75b: mahatyā kakṣayā bhāgā mahānto +alpās tathālpayā//
body.translated_text: One human year is one day of the gods; thirty of those are a month; twelve months are a divine year. //

body.text:
12.76a: kālenālpena bhagaṇaṃ bhuṅkte +alpabhramaṇāśritaH/
12.76b: grahaH kālena mahatā maṇḍale mahati bhraman//
body.translated_text: Twelve thousand divine years are one <s>caturyuga</s>; one thousand of those are a day of <s>Brahmā</s>; a night of <s>Brahmā</s> is the same. //

body.text:
12.77a: svalpayāto bahūn bhuṅkte bhagaṇān śītadīdhitiH/
12.77b: mahatyā kakṣayā gacchan tataH svalpaṃ śanaiścaraH//
body.translated_text: At the beginning of the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, creation proceeds; at the beginning of the night, dissolution. The age of <s>Brahmā</s> is one hundred [of his] years; half has elapsed. //

body.text:
12.78a: mandād adhaH krameṇa syuś caturthā divasādhipāH/
12.78b: varṣādhipatayas tadvat tṛtīyāś ca prakīrtitāH//
body.translated_text: From the remaining half, this first day is in progress; of that day, six <s>Manus</s> have passed. //

body.text:
12.79a: ūrdhvakrameṇa śaśino *māsānām adhipāH smṛtāH/(ḍ masānām)
12.79b: horeśāH sūryatanayād adho+adhaH kramaśas tathā//
body.translated_text: The present is the seventh, <s>Vaivasvata</s>; of his reign, twenty-seven <s>caturyugas</s> have passed. //

body.text:
12.80a: bhaved bhakakṣā tīkṣṇāṃśor bhramaṇaṃ ṣaṣṭitāḍitam/
12.80b: sarvopariṣṭād bhramati yojanais tair bhamaṇḍalam//
body.translated_text: Of the twenty-eighth, three <s>yugas</s> have passed; the current [yuga] is the <s>Kali</s>, in which [this text was revealed]. //

body.text:
12.81a: kalpoktacandrabhagaṇā guṇitāH śaśikakṣayā/
12.81b: ākāśakakṣā sā jñeyā karavyāptis tathā raveH//
body.translated_text: From the creation [to the present epoch], the elapsed years are 1,953,720,000 (one billion, nine hundred fifty-three million, seven hundred twenty thousand). //

body.text:
12.82a: saiva yatkalpabhagaṇair bhaktā tadbhramaṇaṃ bhavet/
12.82b: kuvāsarair vibhajyāhnaH sarveṣāṃ prāggatiH smṛtā//
body.translated_text: This is the number of years elapsed from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> to the end of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>. From that, compute the positions of the planets and their <s>ucca</s>, <s>pāta</s>, and the rest. //

body.text:
12.83a: bhuktiyojanajā saṅkhyā sendor bhramaṇasaṅguṇā/
12.83b: svakakṣāptā tu sā tasya tithyāptā gatiliptikā//
body.translated_text: [Chapter 13: On Instruments and Miscellaneous:] Now I shall explain the instruments for ascertaining the directions, place, and time. //

body.text:
12.84a: kakṣā bhūkarṇaguṇitā mahīmaṇḍalabhājitā/
12.84b: tatkarṇā bhūmikarṇonā grahoccyaṃ svaṃ dalīkṛtāH//
body.translated_text: Having made a level circular surface (<s>maṇḍala</s>), place a gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>) at its center, perpendicular, [and observe] the shadow tips to determine the east-west line. //

body.text:
12.85a: khatrayābdhidvidahanāH kakṣā tu himadīdhiteH/(32430
12.85b: jñaśīghrasyāṅkakhadvitritkṛtaśūnyendavas tathā//(1043209)
body.translated_text: From that, the north-south line is perpendicular. With these two lines, the intermediate directions are established. //

body.text:
12.86a: śukraśīghrasya saptāgnirasābdhirasaṣaḍyamāH/(2664637)
12.86b: tato +arkabudhaśukrāṇāṃ khakhārthaikasurārṇavāH//(4331500)
body.translated_text: The shadow at noon, divided by twelve [the gnomon's height], gives the tangent of the latitude. From the arc of that, one's latitude is known. //

body.text:
12.87a: kujasyāpy aṅkaśūnyāṅkaṣaḍvedaikabhujaṅgamāH/(8146909)
12.87b: candroccasya kṛtāṣṭābdhivasudvitryaṣṭavahnayaH//(38328484)
body.translated_text: When the Sun is on the equator, the shadow at noon points exactly north-south and its length, multiplied by twelve, gives the gnomon-shadow ratio. //

body.text:
12.88a: kṛtartumunipañcādriguṇenduviṣayā guroH/(51375764)
12.88b: svarbhānor vedatarkāṣṭadviśailārthakhakuñjarāH//(80572864)
body.translated_text: From the gnomon-tip shadow-circle and the equation of time, one computes the true local time. //

body.text:
12.89a: pañcavāṇākṣināgarturasādryarkāH śanes tataH/(127668255)
12.89b: bhānāṃ ravikhaśūnyāṅkavasurandhraśarāśvinaH//(25980012)
body.translated_text: The time before and after noon is determined from the shadow lengths, [using] the latitude and declination. //

body.text:
12.90a: khavyomakhatrayakhasāgraṣaṭkanāgavyomāṣṭaśūnyayamarūpanagāṣṭacandrāH/(18712080864000000)
12.90b: brahmāṇḍasampuṭaparibhramaṇaṃ samantād abhyantare dinakarasya karaprasāraH//
body.translated_text: The <s>nāḍīs</s> elapsed since sunrise or remaining until sunset are computed from the hour-angle. //

body.text:
[jyotiṣopaniṣad]
13.01a: atha gupte śucau deśe snātaH śucir alaṅkṛtaH/
13.01b: sampūjya bhāskaraṃ bhaktyā grahān bhāny atha guhyakān//
body.translated_text: The difference of the ascensional difference values gives the duration of the twilight in <s>nāḍīs</s>. //

body.text:
13.02a: pāramparyopadeśena yathājñānaṃ guror mukhāt/
13.02b: ācāryaH śiṣyabodhārthaṃ sarvaṃ pratyakṣadarśivān//
body.translated_text: An armillary sphere (<s>gola</s>-instrument) should be made with rings for the ecliptic, equator, horizon, and meridian, mounted so as to rotate about the polar axis. //

body.text:
13.03a: bhūbhagolasya racanāṃ kuryād āścaryakāriṇīm/
13.03b: abhīṣṭaṃ pṛthivīgolaṃ kārayitvā tu dāravam//
body.translated_text: Place the Sun's marker on the ecliptic; rotate the sphere; the rising and setting points and shadow lengths will correspond to observation. //

body.text:
13.04a: daṇḍaṃ tanmadhyagaṃ meror ubhayatra vinirgatam/
13.04b: ādhārakakṣādvitayaṃ kakṣā vaiṣuvatī tathā//
body.translated_text: The equatorial ring should bear the hours; the ecliptic ring, the degrees of the signs. //

body.text:
13.05a: bhagaṇāṃśāṅgulaiH kāryā dalitais tisra eva tāH/
13.05b: svāhorātrārdhakarṇaiś ca tatpramāṇānumānataH//
body.translated_text: A <s>cakra</s>-instrument (disk) is made flat, with graduated degrees around the circumference; a pivoting sighting bar [is attached at the center]. //

body.text:
13.06a: krāntivikṣepabhāgaiś ca dalitair dakṣiṇottaraiH/
13.06b: svaiH svair apakramais tisro meṣādīnām apakramāt//
body.translated_text: Aiming at a planet through both sights [on the bar], one reads the altitude from the graduated arc. //

body.text:
13.07a: kakṣāH prakalpayet tāś ca karkyādīnāṃ viparyayāt/
13.07b: tadvat tisras tulādīnāṃ mṛgādīnāṃ vilomataH//
body.translated_text: From the observed altitude, the zenith distance is known; from that, the declination, right ascension, and longitude of the planet. //

body.text:
13.08a: yāmyagolāśritāH kāryāH kakṣādhārād dvayor api/
13.08b: yāmyodaggolasaṃsthānāṃ bhānām abhijitas tathā//
body.translated_text: For computing the positions of the Moon and planets, one observes them when near a known star. //

body.text:
13.09a: saptarṣīṇām agastyasya brahmādīnāṃ ca kalpayet/
13.09b: madhye vaiṣuvatī kakṣā sarveṣām eva saṃsthitā//
body.translated_text: The angular distance from the known star gives the planet's longitude correction. //

body.text:
13.10a: tadādhārayuter ūrdhvam ayane viṣuvadvayam/
13.10b: viṣuvatsthānato bhāgaiH sphuṭair bhagaṇasañcarāt//
body.translated_text: This is the secret knowledge for the observation of celestial bodies. //

body.text:
13.11a: kṣetrāṇy evam ajādīnāṃ tiryagjyābhiH prakalpayet/
13.11b: ayanād ayanaṃ caiva kakṣā tiryak tathāparā//
body.translated_text: The <s>kartarī</s>-instrument (scissors), consisting of two bars joined at a pivot, is used for measuring angular distances between two celestial objects. //

body.text:
13.12a: krāntisañjñā tayā sūryaH sadā paryeti bhāsayan/
13.12b: candrādyāś ca svakaiH pātair apamaṇḍalam āśritaiH//
body.translated_text: The sighting is performed toward the two objects simultaneously; the angle between the bars, measured against the graduated arc, gives the angular separation. //

body.text:
13.13a: tato +apakṛṣṭā dṛśyante vikṣepānteṣv apakramāt/
13.13b: udayakṣitije lagnam astaṃ gacchac ca tadvaśāt//
body.translated_text: A water clock should be made from a copper vessel with a hole at the bottom; place it in pure water — it sinks sixty times in a day and night. //

body.text:
13.14a: laṅkodayair yathāsiddhaṃ khamadhyopari madhyamam/
13.14b: madhyakṣitijayor madhye yā jyā sāntyābhidhīyate//
body.translated_text: The Sun's position at any time can be verified by the shadow cast by the gnomon, confirming the computed values. //

body.text:
13.15a: jñeyā caradalajyā ca viṣuvat kṣitijāntaram/
13.15b: kṛtvopari svakaṃ sthānaṃ madhye kṣitijamaṇḍalam//
body.translated_text: For the measurement of time at night, one uses the <s>nakṣatras</s>; their transit at the meridian indicates the elapsed portion of the night. //

body.text:
13.16a: vastracchannaṃ bahis cāpi lokālokena veṣṭitam/
13.16b: amṛtasrāvayogena kālabhramaṇasādhanam//
body.translated_text: The rising times of the <s>nakṣatras</s>, previously stated, serve as the standard for night-time measurement. //

body.text:
13.17a: tuṅgabījasamāyuktaṃ golayantraṃ prasādhayet/
13.17b: gopyam etat prakāśoktaṃ sarvagamyaṃ bhaved iha//
body.translated_text: When the computed and observed positions agree, the astronomer's work is confirmed. //

body.text:
13.18a: tasmād gurūpadeśena racayed golam uttamam/
13.18b: yuge yuge samucchinnā racaneyaṃ vivasvataH//
body.translated_text: When they disagree, one should examine the parameters and correct them by observation. //

body.text:
13.19a: prasādāt kasyacid bhūyaH prādur bhavati kāmataH/
13.19b: kālasaṃsādhanārthāya tathā yantrāṇi sādhayet//
body.translated_text: The wise astronomer, verifying computations against observations over time, perfects the science. //

body.text:
13.20a: ekākī yojayed bījaṃ yantre vismayakāriṇi/
13.20b: śaṅkuyaṣṭidhanuścakraiś chāyāyantrair anekadhā//
body.translated_text: This system of the <s>Sūryasiddhānta</s>, taught by the Sun himself, is the most accurate for determining planetary positions. //

body.text:
13.21a: gurūpadeśād vijñeyaṃ kālajñānam atandritaiH/
13.21b: toyayantrakapālādyair mayūranaravānaraiH//
body.translated_text: Other systems, being partial versions, are subordinate to this one. //

body.text: 13.21c: sasūtrareṇugarbhaiś ca samyak kālaṃ prasādhayet//
body.translated_text: The astronomer who masters this <s>siddhānta</s> knows the past, present, and future motions of all celestial bodies. //

body.text:
13.22a: pāradārāmbusūtrāṇi śulvatailajalāni ca/
13.22b: bījāni pāṃsavas teṣu prayogās te +api durlabhāH//
body.translated_text: Through this knowledge of the celestial sphere (<s>gola</s>) and planetary motion, one attains the knowledge pleasing to the gods. //

body.text:
13.23a: tāṃrapātram adhaśchidraṃ nyastaṃ kuṇḍe +amalāmbhasi/
13.23b: ṣaṣṭir majjaty ahorātre sphuṭaṃ yantraṃ kapālakam//
body.translated_text: A copper vessel with a hole at the bottom, placed in a basin of pure water — it sinks sixty times in a day and night; this is the accurate instrument called <s>kapālaka</s>. //

body.text:
13.24a: narayantraṃ tathā sādhu divā ca vimale ravau/
13.24b: chāyāsaṃsādhanaiH proktaṃ kālasādhanam uttamam//
body.translated_text: Likewise, the human-instrument (<s>narayantra</s>) [i.e., the shadow of a person] is good by day when the Sun is clear; the methods of shadow-measurement have been declared as the supreme means of determining time. //

body.text:
13.25a: grahanakṣatracaritaṃ jñātvā golaṃ ca tattvataH/
13.25b: grahalokam avāpnoti paryāyeṇātmavān naraH//
body.translated_text: Having truly known the movements of planets and stars and the celestial sphere, a self-possessed person attains the world of the planets in due course. //

body.text:
[māna]
14.01a: brāhmaṃ divyaṃ tathā pitryaṃ prājāpatyaṃ guros tathā/
14.01b: sauraṃ ca sāvanaṃ cāndram ārkṣaṃ mānāni vai nava//

14.02a: caturbhir vyavahāro +atra sauracāndrārkṣasāvanaiH/
14.02b: bārhaspatyena ṣaṣṭyabdaṃ jñeyaṃ nānyais tu nityaśaH//

14.03a: saureṇa dyuniśor mānaṃ ṣaḍaśītimukhāni ca/
14.03b: ayanaṃ viṣuvaccaiva saṃkrānteH puṇyakālatā//

14.04a: tulādi ṣaḍaśītyahnāṃ ṣaḍaśītimukhaṃ kramāt/
14.04b: taccatuṣṭayam eva syād dvisvabhāveṣu rāśiṣu//

14.05a: ṣaḍviṃśe dhanuṣo bhāge dvāviṃśe nimiṣasya ca/
14.05b: mithunāṣṭādaśe bhāge kanyāyās tu caturdaśa//

14.06a: tataH śeṣāṇi kanyāyā yāny ahāni tu ṣoḍaśa/
14.06b: kratubhis tāni tulyāni pitṝṇāṃ dattam akṣayam//

14.07a: bhacakranābhau viṣuvaddvitayaṃ samasūtragam/
14.07b: ayanadvitayaṃ caiva catasraH prathitās tu tāH//

14.08a: tadantareṣu saṃkrāntidvitayaṃ dvitayaṃ punaH/
14.08b: nairantaryāt tu saṃkrānter jñeyaṃ viṣṇupadīdvayam//

14.09a: bhānor makarasaṅkrānteH ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam/
14.09b: karkyādes tu tathaiva syāt ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam//

14.10a: dvirāśinātha ṛtavas tato +api śiśirādayaH/
14.10b: meṣādayo dvādaśaite māsās tair eva vatsaraH//

14.11a: arkamānakalāH ṣaṣṭyā guṇitā bhuktibhājitāH/
14.11b: tadardhanāḍyaH saṅkrānter arvāk puṇyaṃ tathā pare//

14.12a: arkād viniHsṛtaH prācīṃ yad yāty aharahaH śaśī/
14.12b: tac cāndramānam aṃśais tu jñeyā dvādaśabhis tithiH//

14.13a: tithiH karaṇam udvāhaH kṣauraṃ sarvakriyās tathā/
14.13b: vratopavāsayātrāṇāṃ kriyā cāndreṇa gṛhyate//

14.14a: triṃśatā tithibhir māsaś cāndraH pitryam ahaH smṛtam/
14.14b: niśā ca māsapakṣāntau tayor madhye vibhāgataH//

14.15a: bhacakrabhramaṇaṃ nityaṃ nākṣatraṃ dinam ucyate/
14.15b: nakṣatranāmnā māsās tu jñeyāH parvāntayogataH//

14.16a: kārtikyādiṣu saṃyoge kṛttikādi dvayaṃ dvayam/
14.16b: antyopāntyau pañcamaś ca tridhā māsatrayaṃ smṛtam//

14.17a: vaiśākhādiṣu kṛṣṇe ca yogaH pañcadaśe tithau/
14.17b: kārttikādīni varṣāṇi guror astodayāt tathā//

14.18a: udayād udayaṃ bhānoH sāvanaṃ tat prakīrtitam/
14.18b: sāvanāni syur *etena yajñakālavidhis tu taiH//(ḍ etana)

14.19a: sūtakādiparicchedo dinamāsābdapās tathā/
14.19b: madhyamā grahabhuktis tu sāvanenaiva gṛhyate//

14.20a: surāsurāṇām anyonyam ahorātraṃ viparyayāt/
14.20b: yatproktaṃ tad bhaved divyaṃ bhānor bhagaṇapūraṇāt//

14.21a: manvantaravyavasthā ca prājāpatyam udāhṛtam/
14.21b: na tatra dyuniśor bhedo brāhmaṃ kalpaH prakīrtitam//

14.22a: etat te paramākhyātaṃ rahasyaṃ paramādbhutam/
14.22b: brahmaitat paramaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam//

14.23a: divyaṃ cārkṣaṃ grahāṇāṃ ca darśitaṃ jñānam uttamam/
14.23b: vijñāyārkādilokeṣu sthānaṃ prāpnoti śāsvatam//

14.24a: ity uktvā mayam āmantrya samyak tenābhipūjitaH/
14.24b: divam ācakrame +arkāṃśaH praviveśa svamaṇḍalam//

14.25a: mayo +atha divyaṃ tajñānaṃ jñātvā sākṣād vivasvataH/
14.25b: kṛtakṛtyam ivātmānaṃ mene nirdhūtakalmaṣam//

14.26a: jñātvā tam ṛṣayaś cātha sūryalabdhavaraṃ mayam/
14.26b: paribabrur upetyātho jñānaṃ papracchur ādarāt//

14.27a: sa tebhyaH pradadau prīto grahāṇāṃ caritaṃ mahat/
14.27b: atyadbhutatamaṃ loke rahasyaṃ brahmasammitam//
